content.english: Come let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.

content.latin: Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
content.english: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

content.latin: Ant. Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. O come, let us worship.

segments.t: Ant.
Veníte, adorémus.

content.latin: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius (genuflectitur) veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
content.english: For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. (genuflect) Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

segments.t: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius

content.latin: Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
content.english: Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.

content.latin: Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
content.english: Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

content.english: Psalm 61 [1]

segments.t: Psalmus 61

content.latin: 61:2 Nonne Deo subiécta erit ánima mea? * ab ipso enim salutáre meum.
content.english: 61:2 Shall not my soul be subject to God? * for from him is my salvation.

segments.t: Nonne Deo subiécta erit ánima mea? * ab ipso enim salutáre meum.

content.latin: 61:3 Nam et ipse Deus meus, et salutáris meus: * suscéptor meus, non movébor ámplius.
content.english: 61:3 For he is my God and my saviour: * he is my protector, I shall be moved no more.

segments.t: Nam et ipse Deus meus, et salutáris meus: * suscéptor meus, non movébor ámplius.

content.latin: 61:4 Quoúsque irrúitis in hóminem? * interfícitis univérsi vos: tamquam paríeti inclináto et macériæ depúlsæ?
content.english: 61:4 How long do you rush in upon a man? * you all kill, as if you were thrusting down a leaning wall, and a tottering fence.

segments.t: Quoúsque irrúitis in hóminem? * interfícitis univérsi vos: tamquam paríeti inclináto et macériæ depúlsæ?

content.latin: 61:5 Verúmtamen prétium meum cogitavérunt repéllere, cucúrri in siti: * ore suo benedicébant, et corde suo maledicébant.
content.english: 61:5 But they have thought to cast away my price; I ran in thirst: * they blessed with their mouth, but cursed with their heart.

segments.t: Verúmtamen prétium meum cogitavérunt repéllere, cucúrri in siti: * ore suo benedicébant, et corde suo maledicébant.

content.latin: 61:6 Verúmtamen Deo subiécta esto, ánima mea: * quóniam ab ipso patiéntia mea.
content.english: 61:6 But be thou, O my soul, subject to God: * for from him is my patience.

segments.t: Verúmtamen Deo subiécta esto, ánima mea: * quóniam ab ipso patiéntia mea.

content.latin: 61:7 Quia ipse Deus meus, et salvátor meus: * adiútor meus, non emigrábo.
content.english: 61:7 For he is my God and my saviour: * he is my helper, I shall not be moved.

segments.t: Quia ipse Deus meus, et salvátor meus: * adiútor meus, non emigrábo.

content.latin: 61:8 In Deo salutáre meum, et glória mea: * Deus auxílii mei, et spes mea in Deo est.
content.english: 61:8 In God is my salvation and my glory: * he is the God of my help, and my hope is in God.

segments.t: In Deo salutáre meum, et glória mea: * Deus auxílii mei, et spes mea in Deo est.

content.latin: 61:9 Speráte in eo omnis congregátio pópuli, effúndite coram illo corda vestra: * Deus adiútor noster in ætérnum.
content.english: 61:9 Trust in him, all ye congregation of people: pour out your hearts before him. * God is our helper for ever.

segments.t: Speráte in eo omnis congregátio pópuli, effúndite coram illo corda vestra: * Deus adiútor noster in ætérnum.

content.latin: 61:10 Verúmtamen vani fílii hóminum, mendáces fílii hóminum in statéris: * ut decípiant ipsi de vanitáte in idípsum.
content.english: 61:10 But vain are the sons of men, the sons of men are liars in the balances: * that by vanity they may together deceive.

segments.t: Verúmtamen vani fílii hóminum, mendáces fílii hóminum in statéris: * ut decípiant ipsi de vanitáte in idípsum.

content.latin: 61:11 Nolíte speráre in iniquitáte, et rapínas nolíte concupíscere: * divítiæ si áffluant, nolíte cor appónere.
content.english: 61:11 Trust not in iniquity, and cover not robberies: * if riches abound, set not your heart upon them.

segments.t: Nolíte speráre in iniquitáte, et rapínas nolíte concupíscere: * divítiæ si áffluant, nolíte cor appónere.

content.latin: 61:12 Semel locútus est Deus, duo hæc audívi, quia potéstas Dei est, et tibi, Dómine, misericórdia: * quia tu reddes unicuíque iuxta ópera sua.
content.english: 61:12 God hath spoken once, these two things have I heard, that power belongeth to God, and mercy to thee, O Lord; * for thou wilt render to every man according to his works.

segments.t: Semel locútus est Deus, duo hæc audívi, quia potéstas Dei est, et tibi, Dómine, misericórdia: * quia tu reddes unicuíque iuxta ópera sua.

Psalmus 65(1-12)

content.latin: 65:1 Iubiláte Deo, omnis terra, psalmum dícite nómini eius: * date glóriam laudi eius.
content.english: 65:1 Shout with joy to God, all the earth, sing ye a psalm to his name; * give glory to his praise.

segments.t: Iubiláte Deo, omnis terra, psalmum dícite nómini eius: * date glóriam laudi eius.

content.latin: 65:3 Dícite Deo: Quam terribília sunt ópera tua, Dómine! * in multitúdine virtútis tuæ mentiéntur tibi inimíci tui.
content.english: 65:3 Say unto God, How terrible are thy works, O Lord! * in the multitude of thy strength thy enemies shall lie to thee.

segments.t: Dícite Deo: Quam terribília sunt ópera tua, Dómine! * in multitúdine virtútis tuæ mentiéntur tibi inimíci tui.

content.latin: 65:4 Omnis terra adóret te, et psallat tibi: * psalmum dicat nómini tuo.
content.english: 65:4 Let all the earth adore thee, * and sing to thee: let it sing a psalm to thy name.

segments.t: Omnis terra adóret te, et psallat tibi: * psalmum dicat nómini tuo.

content.latin: 65:5 Veníte, et vidéte ópera Dei: * terríbilis in consíliis super fílios hóminum.
content.english: 65:5 Come and see the works of God; * who is terrible in his counsels over the sons of men.

segments.t: Veníte, et vidéte ópera Dei: * terríbilis in consíliis super fílios hóminum.

content.latin: 65:6 Qui convértit mare in áridam, in flúmine pertransíbunt pede: * ibi lætábimur in ipso.
content.english: 65:6 Who turneth the sea into dry land, in the river they shall pass on foot: * there shall we rejoice in him.

segments.t: Qui convértit mare in áridam, in flúmine pertransíbunt pede: * ibi lætábimur in ipso.

content.latin: 65:7 Qui dominátur in virtúte sua in ætérnum, óculi eius super gentes respíciunt: * qui exásperant non exalténtur in semetípsis.
content.english: 65:7 Who by his power ruleth for ever: his eyes behold the nations; * let not them that provoke him be exalted in themselves.

segments.t: Qui dominátur in virtúte sua in ætérnum, óculi eius super gentes respíciunt: * qui exásperant non exalténtur in semetípsis.

content.latin: 65:8 Benedícite, gentes, Deum nostrum: * et audítam fácite vocem laudis eius,
content.english: 65:8 O bless our God, ye Gentiles: * and make the voice of his praise to be heard.

segments.t: Benedícite, gentes, Deum nostrum: * et audítam fácite vocem laudis eius,

content.latin: 65:9 Qui pósuit ánimam meam ad vitam: * et non dedit in commotiónem pedes meos.
content.english: 65:9 Who hath set my soul to live: * and hath not suffered my feet to be moved:

segments.t: Qui pósuit ánimam meam ad vitam: * et non dedit in commotiónem pedes meos.

content.latin: 65:10 Quóniam probásti nos, Deus: * igne nos examinásti, sicut examinátur argéntum.
content.english: 65:10 For thou, O God, hast proved us: * thou hast tried us by fire, as silver is tried.

segments.t: Quóniam probásti nos, Deus: * igne nos examinásti, sicut examinátur argéntum.

content.latin: 65:11 Induxísti nos in láqueum, posuísti tribulatiónes in dorso nostro: * imposuísti hómines super cápita nostra.
content.english: 65:11 Thou hast brought us into a net, thou hast laid afflictions on our back: * thou hast set men over our heads.

segments.t: Induxísti nos in láqueum, posuísti tribulatiónes in dorso nostro: * imposuísti hómines super cápita nostra.

content.latin: 65:12 Transívimus per ignem et aquam: * et eduxísti nos in refrigérium.
content.english: 65:12 We have passed through fire and water, * and thou hast brought us out into a refreshment.

segments.t: Transívimus per ignem et aquam: * et eduxísti nos in refrigérium.

content.latin: 65:13 Introíbo in domum tuam in holocáustis: * reddam tibi vota mea, quæ distinxérunt lábia mea.
content.english: 65:13 I will go into thy house with burnt offerings: * I will pay thee my vows, which my lips have uttered,

content.english: 65:15 I will offer up to thee holocausts full of marrow, with burnt offerings of rams: * I will offer to thee bullocks with goats.

segments.t: Holocáusta medulláta ófferam tibi cum incénso aríetum: * ófferam tibi boves cum hircis.

content.latin: 65:16 Veníte, audíte, et narrábo, omnes, qui timétis Deum: * quanta fecit ánimæ meæ.
content.english: 65:16 Come and hear, all ye that fear God, * and I will tell you what great things he hath done for my soul.

segments.t: Veníte, audíte, et narrábo, omnes, qui timétis Deum: * quanta fecit ánimæ meæ.

content.latin: 65:17 Ad ipsum ore meo clamávi, * et exaltávi sub lingua mea.
content.english: 65:17 I cried to him with my mouth: * and I extolled him with my tongue.

segments.t: Ad ipsum ore meo clamávi, * et exaltávi sub lingua mea.

content.latin: 65:18 Iniquitátem si aspéxi in corde meo, * non exáudiet Dóminus.

segments.t: Iniquitátem si aspéxi in corde meo, * non exáudiet Dóminus.

content.latin: 65:19 Proptérea exaudívit Deus, * et atténdit voci deprecatiónis meæ.
content.english: 65:19 Therefore hath God heard me, * and hath attended to the voice of my supplication.

content.latin: 65:20 Benedíctus Deus, * qui non amóvit oratiónem meam, et misericórdiam suam a me.

et fúgiant qui odérunt eum, a fácie eius.

content.latin: 67:3 Sicut déficit fumus, defíciant: * sicut fluit cera a fácie ignis, sic péreant peccatóres a fácie Dei.
content.english: 67:3 As smoke vanisheth, so let them vanish away: * as wax melteth before the fire, so let the wicked perish at the presence of God.

segments.t: Sicut déficit fumus, defíciant: * sicut fluit cera a fácie ignis, sic péreant peccatóres a fácie Dei.

content.latin: 67:4 Et iusti epuléntur, et exsúltent in conspéctu Dei: * et delecténtur in lætítia.
content.english: 67:4 And let the just feast, and rejoice before God: * and be delighted with gladness.

segments.t: Et iusti epuléntur, et exsúltent in conspéctu Dei: * et delecténtur in lætítia.

content.latin: 67:5 Cantáte Deo, psalmum dícite nómini eius: * iter fácite ei, qui ascéndit super occásum: (fit reverentia) Dóminus nomen illi.
content.english: 67:5 Sing ye to God, sing a psalm to his name, * make a way for him who ascendeth upon the west: (bow head) the Lord is his name.

segments.t: Cantáte Deo, psalmum dícite nómini eius: * iter fácite ei, qui ascéndit super occásum:
(fit reverentia)
Dóminus nomen illi.

content.latin: 67:5 Exsultáte in conspéctu eius: * turbabúntur a fácie eius, patris orphanórum et iúdicis viduárum.
content.english: 67:5 Rejoice ye before him: * but the wicked shall be troubled at his presence, who is the father of orphans, and the judge of widows.

segments.t: Exsultáte in conspéctu eius: * turbabúntur a fácie eius, patris orphanórum et iúdicis viduárum.

content.latin: 67:6 Deus in loco sancto suo: * Deus, qui inhabitáre facit uníus moris in domo:
content.english: 67:6 God in his holy place: * God who maketh men of one manner to dwell in a house:

segments.t: Deus in loco sancto suo: * Deus, qui inhabitáre facit uníus moris in domo:

content.latin: 67:7 Qui edúcit vinctos in fortitúdine, * simíliter eos qui exásperant, qui hábitant in sepúlcris.
content.english: 67:7 Who bringeth out them that were bound in strength; * in like manner them that provoke, that dwell in sepulchres.

segments.t: Qui edúcit vinctos in fortitúdine, * simíliter eos qui exásperant, qui hábitant in sepúlcris.

content.latin: 67:8 Deus, cum egrederéris in conspéctu pópuli tui, * cum pertransíres in desérto:
content.english: 67:8 O God, when thou didst go forth in the sight of thy people, * when thou didst pass through the desert:

segments.t: Deus, cum egrederéris in conspéctu pópuli tui, * cum pertransíres in desérto:

content.latin: 67:9 Terra mota est, étenim cæli distillavérunt a fácie Dei Sínai, * a fácie Dei Israël.
content.english: 67:9 The earth was moved, and the heavens dropped at the presence of the God of Sinai, * at the presence of the God of Israel.

segments.t: Terra mota est, étenim cæli distillavérunt a fácie Dei Sínai, * a fácie Dei Israël.

content.latin: 67:10 Plúviam voluntáriam segregábis, Deus, hereditáti tuæ: * et infirmáta est, tu vero perfecísti eam.
content.english: 67:10 Thou shalt set aside for thy inheritance a free rain, * O God: and it was weakened, but thou hast made it perfect.

segments.t: Plúviam voluntáriam segregábis, Deus, hereditáti tuæ: * et infirmáta est, tu vero perfecísti eam.

content.latin: 67:11 Animália tua habitábunt in ea: * parásti in dulcédine tua páuperi, Deus.
content.english: 67:11 In it shall thy animals dwell; * in thy sweetness, O God, thou hast provided for the poor.

segments.t: Animália tua habitábunt in ea: * parásti in dulcédine tua páuperi, Deus.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Exsúrgat Deus, et dissipéntur inimíci eius.
content.english: Ant. Let God arise, and let his enemies be scattered.

segments.t: Ant.
Exsúrgat Deus, et dissipéntur inimíci eius.

content.latin: Ant. Deus noster, * Deus salvos faciéndi: et Dómini sunt éxitus mortis.
content.english: Ant. Our God * is the God of salvation: and the Lord of the issues from death.

segments.t: Ant.
Deus noster, * Deus salvos faciéndi: et Dómini sunt éxitus mortis.
Psalmus 67(12-24)

content.latin: 67:12 Dóminus dabit verbum evangelizántibus, * virtúte multa.
content.english: 67:12 The Lord shall give the word to them that preach good tidings, * with great power.

segments.t: Dóminus dabit verbum evangelizántibus, * virtúte multa.

content.latin: 67:13 Rex virtútum dilécti, dilécti: * et speciéi domus divídere spólia.
content.english: 67:13 The king of powers is of the beloved, * of the beloved; and the beauty of the house shall divide spoils.

segments.t: Rex virtútum dilécti, dilécti: * et speciéi domus divídere spólia.

content.latin: 67:14 Si dormiátis inter médios cleros, pennæ colúmbæ deargentátæ, * et posterióra dorsi eius in pallóre auri.
content.english: 67:14 If you sleep among the midst of lots, you shall be as the wings of a dove covered with silver, * and the hinder parts of her back with the paleness of gold.

segments.t: Si dormiátis inter médios cleros, pennæ colúmbæ deargentátæ, * et posterióra dorsi eius in pallóre auri.

content.latin: 67:15 Dum discérnit cæléstis reges super eam, nive dealbabúntur in Selmon: * mons Dei, mons pinguis.
content.english: 67:15 When he that is in heaven appointeth kings over her, they shall be whited with snow in Selmon. * The mountain of God is a fat mountain,

segments.t: Dum discérnit cæléstis reges super eam, nive dealbabúntur in Selmon: * mons Dei, mons pinguis.

content.latin: 67:16 Mons coagulátus, mons pinguis: * ut quid suspicámini montes coagulátos?
content.english: 67:16 a curdled mountain, a fat mountain; * Why suspect, ye curdled mountains?

segments.t: Mons coagulátus, mons pinguis: * ut quid suspicámini montes coagulátos?

content.latin: 67:17 Mons, in quo beneplácitum est Deo habitáre in eo: * étenim Dóminus habitábit in finem.
content.english: 67:17 A mountain in which God is well pleased to dwell: * for there the Lord shall dwell unto the end.

segments.t: Mons, in quo beneplácitum est Deo habitáre in eo: * étenim Dóminus habitábit in finem.

content.latin: 67:18 Currus Dei decem míllibus múltiplex, míllia lætántium: * Dóminus in eis in Sina in sancto.
content.english: 67:18 The chariot of God is attended by ten thousands; thousands of them that rejoice: * the Lord is among them in Sinai, in the holy place.

segments.t: Currus Dei decem míllibus múltiplex, míllia lætántium: * Dóminus in eis in Sina in sancto.

content.latin: 67:19 Ascendísti in altum, cepísti captivitátem: * accepísti dona in homínibus.
content.english: 67:19 Thou hast ascended on high, thou hast led captivity captive; * thou hast received gifts in men.

segments.t: Ascendísti in altum, cepísti captivitátem: * accepísti dona in homínibus.

content.latin: 67:19 Étenim non credéntes, * inhabitáre Dóminum Deum.
content.english: 67:19 Yea for those also that do not believe, * the dwelling of the Lord God.

segments.t: Étenim non credéntes, * inhabitáre Dóminum Deum.

content.latin: 67:20 Benedíctus Dóminus die cotídie: * prósperum iter fáciet nobis Deus salutárium nostrórum.
content.english: 67:20 Blessed be the Lord day by day: * the God of our salvation will make our journey prosperous to us.

segments.t: Benedíctus Dóminus die cotídie: * prósperum iter fáciet nobis Deus salutárium nostrórum.

content.latin: 67:21 Deus noster, Deus salvos faciéndi: * et Dómini Dómini éxitus mortis.
content.english: 67:21 Our God is the God of salvation: * and of the Lord, of the Lord are the issues from death.

segments.t: Deus noster, Deus salvos faciéndi: * et Dómini Dómini éxitus mortis.

content.latin: 67:22 Verúmtamen Deus confrínget cápita inimicórum suórum: * vérticem capílli perambulántium in delíctis suis.
content.english: 67:22 But God shall break the heads of his enemies: * the hairy crown of them that walk on in their sins.

segments.t: Verúmtamen Deus confrínget cápita inimicórum suórum: * vérticem capílli perambulántium in delíctis suis.

content.latin: 67:23 Dixit Dóminus: Ex Basan convértam, * convértam in profúndum maris:
content.english: 67:23 The Lord said: I will turn them from Basan, * I will turn them into the depth of the sea:

segments.t: Dixit Dóminus: Ex Basan convértam, * convértam in profúndum maris:

content.latin: 67:24 Ut intingátur pes tuus in sánguine: * lingua canum tuórum ex inimícis, ab ipso.
content.english: 67:24 That thy foot may be dipped in the blood of thy enemies; * the tongue of thy dogs be red with the same.

segments.t: Ut intingátur pes tuus in sánguine: * lingua canum tuórum ex inimícis, ab ipso.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Deus noster, Deus salvos faciéndi: et Dómini sunt éxitus mortis.
content.english: Ant. Our God is the God of salvation: and the Lord of the issues from death.

segments.t: Ant.
Deus noster, Deus salvos faciéndi: et Dómini sunt éxitus mortis.

content.latin: Ant. In ecclésiis * benedícite Dómino Deo.
content.english: Ant. In the churches * bless ye God the Lord.

segments.t: Ant.
In ecclésiis * benedícite Dómino Deo.
Psalmus 67(25-36)

content.latin: 67:25 Vidérunt ingréssus tuos, Deus: * ingréssus Dei mei: regis mei qui est in sancto.
content.english: 67:25 They have seen thy goings, O God, * the goings of my God: of my king who is in his sanctuary.

segments.t: Vidérunt ingréssus tuos, Deus: * ingréssus Dei mei: regis mei qui est in sancto.

content.latin: 67:26 Prævenérunt príncipes coniúncti psalléntibus: * in médio iuvenculárum tympanistriárum.
content.english: 67:26 Princes went before joined with singers, * in the midst of young damsels playing on timbrels.

segments.t: Prævenérunt príncipes coniúncti psalléntibus: * in médio iuvenculárum tympanistriárum.

content.latin: 67:27 In ecclésiis benedícite Deo Dómino, * de fóntibus Israël.
content.english: 67:27 In the churches bless ye God the Lord, * from the fountains of Israel.

segments.t: In ecclésiis benedícite Deo Dómino, * de fóntibus Israël.

content.latin: 67:28 Ibi Béniamin adolescéntulus: * in mentis excéssu.
content.english: 67:28 There is Benjamin a youth, * in ecstasy of mind.

segments.t: Ibi Béniamin adolescéntulus: * in mentis excéssu.

content.latin: 67:28 Príncipes Iuda, duces eórum: * príncipes Zábulon, príncipes Néphtali.
content.english: 67:28 The princes of Juda are their leaders: * the princes of Zabulon, the princes of Nephthali.

segments.t: Príncipes Iuda, duces eórum: * príncipes Zábulon, príncipes Néphtali.

content.latin: 67:29 Manda, Deus, virtúti tuæ: * confírma hoc, Deus, quod operátus es in nobis.
content.english: 67:29 Command thy strength, O God: * confirm, O God, what thou hast wrought in us.

segments.t: Manda, Deus, virtúti tuæ: * confírma hoc, Deus, quod operátus es in nobis.

content.latin: 67:30 A templo tuo in Ierúsalem, * tibi ófferent reges múnera.
content.english: 67:30 From thy temple in Jerusalem, * kings shall offer presents to thee.

segments.t: A templo tuo in Ierúsalem, * tibi ófferent reges múnera.

content.latin: 67:31 Íncrepa feras arúndinis, congregátio taurórum in vaccis populórum: * ut exclúdant eos, qui probáti sunt argénto.
content.english: 67:31 Rebuke the wild beasts of the reeds, the congregation of bulls with the kine of the people; * who seek to exclude them who are tried with silver.

segments.t: Íncrepa feras arúndinis, congregátio taurórum in vaccis populórum: * ut exclúdant eos, qui probáti sunt argénto.

content.latin: 67:31 Díssipa gentes, quæ bella volunt: vénient legáti ex Ægýpto: * Æthiópia prævéniet manus eius Deo.
content.english: 67:31 Scatter thou the nations that delight in wars: ambassadors shall come out of Egypt: * Ethiopia shall soon stretch out her hands to God.

segments.t: Díssipa gentes, quæ bella volunt: vénient legáti ex Ægýpto: * Æthiópia prævéniet manus eius Deo.

content.latin: 67:33 Regna terræ, cantáte Deo: * psállite Dómino.
content.english: 67:33 Sing to God, ye kingdoms of the earth: * sing ye to the Lord:

segments.t: Regna terræ, cantáte Deo: * psállite Dómino.

content.latin: 67:33 Psállite Deo, qui ascéndit super cælum cæli, * ad Oriéntem.
content.english: 67:33 Sing ye to God, who mounteth above the heaven of heavens, * to the east.

segments.t: Psállite Deo, qui ascéndit super cælum cæli, * ad Oriéntem.

content.latin: 67:34 Ecce dabit voci suæ vocem virtútis, date glóriam Deo super Israël, * magnificéntia eius, et virtus eius in núbibus.
content.english: 67:34 Behold he will give to his voice the voice of power: give ye glory to God for Israel, * his magnificence, and his power is in the clouds.

segments.t: Ecce dabit voci suæ vocem virtútis, date glóriam Deo super Israël, * magnificéntia eius, et virtus eius in núbibus.

content.latin: 67:36 Mirábilis Deus in sanctis suis, Deus Israël ipse dabit virtútem, et fortitúdinem plebi suæ, * benedíctus Deus.
content.english: 67:36 God is wonderful in his saints: the God of Israel is he who will give power and strength to his people; * blessed be God.

segments.t: Mirábilis Deus in sanctis suis, Deus Israël ipse dabit virtútem, et fortitúdinem plebi suæ, * benedíctus Deus.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. In ecclésiis benedícite Dómino Deo.
content.english: Ant. In the churches bless ye God the Lord.

segments.t: Ant.
In ecclésiis benedícite Dómino Deo.

content.latin: Ant. Salvum me fac, * Deus, quóniam intravérunt aquæ usque ad ánimam meam. ‡
content.english: Ant. Save me, O God * for the waters are come in even unto my soul. ‡

segments.t: Ant.
Salvum me fac, * Deus, quóniam intravérunt aquæ usque ad ánimam meam.
Psalmus 68(2-13)

content.latin: 68:2 Salvum me fac, Deus: quóniam intravérunt aquæ usque ad ánimam meam.
content.english: 68:2 Save me, O God: for the waters are come in even unto my soul.

segments.t: Salvum me fac, Deus: quóniam intravérunt aquæ usque ad ánimam meam.

content.latin: 68:3 ‡ Infíxus sum in limo profúndi: * et non est substántia.
content.english: 68:3 ‡ I stick fast in the mire of the deep: * and there is no sure standing.

segments.t: Infíxus sum in limo profúndi: * et non est substántia.

content.latin: 68:3 Veni in altitúdinem maris: * et tempéstas demérsit me.
content.english: 68:3 I am come into the depth of the sea: * and a tempest hath overwhelmed me.

segments.t: Veni in altitúdinem maris: * et tempéstas demérsit me.

content.latin: 68:4 Laborávi clamans, raucæ factæ sunt fauces meæ: * defecérunt óculi mei, dum spero in Deum meum.
content.english: 68:4 I have laboured with crying; my jaws are become hoarse: * my eyes have failed, whilst I hope in my God.

segments.t: Laborávi clamans, raucæ factæ sunt fauces meæ: * defecérunt óculi mei, dum spero in Deum meum.

content.latin: 68:5 Multiplicáti sunt super capíllos cápitis mei, * qui odérunt me gratis.
content.english: 68:5 They are multiplied above the hairs of my head, * who hate me without cause.

segments.t: Multiplicáti sunt super capíllos cápitis mei, * qui odérunt me gratis.

content.latin: 68:5 Confortáti sunt qui persecúti sunt me inimíci mei iniúste: * quæ non rápui, tunc exsolvébam.
content.english: 68:5 My enemies are grown strong who have wrongfully persecuted me: * then did I pay that which I took not away.

segments.t: Confortáti sunt qui persecúti sunt me inimíci mei iniúste: * quæ non rápui, tunc exsolvébam.

content.latin: 68:6 Deus, tu scis insipiéntiam meam: * et delícta mea a te non sunt abscóndita.
content.english: 68:6 O God, thou knowest my foolishness; * and my offences are not hidden from thee.

segments.t: Deus, tu scis insipiéntiam meam: * et delícta mea a te non sunt abscóndita.

content.latin: 68:7 Non erubéscant in me qui exspéctant te, Dómine, * Dómine virtútum.
content.english: 68:7 Let not them be ashamed for me, who look for thee, O Lord, * the Lord of hosts.

segments.t: Non erubéscant in me qui exspéctant te, Dómine, * Dómine virtútum.

content.latin: 68:7 Non confundántur super me * qui quærunt te, Deus Israël.
content.english: 68:7 Let them not be confounded on my account, * who seek thee, O God of Israel.

segments.t: Non confundántur super me * qui quærunt te, Deus Israël.

content.latin: 68:8 Quóniam propter te sustínui oppróbrium: * opéruit confúsio fáciem meam.
content.english: 68:8 Because for thy sake I have borne reproach; * shame hath covered my face.

segments.t: Quóniam propter te sustínui oppróbrium: * opéruit confúsio fáciem meam.

content.latin: 68:9 Extráneus factus sum frátribus meis, * et peregrínus fíliis matris meæ.
content.english: 68:9 I am become a stranger to my brethren, * and an alien to the sons of my mother.

segments.t: Extráneus factus sum frátribus meis, * et peregrínus fíliis matris meæ.

content.latin: 68:10 Quóniam zelus domus tuæ comédit me: * et oppróbria exprobrántium tibi cecidérunt super me.
content.english: 68:10 For the zeal of thy house hath eaten me up: * and the reproaches of them that reproached thee are fallen upon me.

segments.t: Quóniam zelus domus tuæ comédit me: * et oppróbria exprobrántium tibi cecidérunt super me.

content.latin: 68:11 Et opérui in ieiúnio ánimam meam: * et factum est in oppróbrium mihi.
content.english: 68:11 And I covered my soul in fasting: * and it was made a reproach to me.

segments.t: Et opérui in ieiúnio ánimam meam: * et factum est in oppróbrium mihi.

content.latin: 68:12 Et pósui vestiméntum meum cilícium: * et factus sum illis in parábolam.
content.english: 68:12 And I made haircloth my garment: * and I became a byword to them.

segments.t: Et pósui vestiméntum meum cilícium: * et factus sum illis in parábolam.

content.latin: 68:13 Advérsum me loquebántur, qui sedébant in porta: * et in me psallébant qui bibébant vinum.
content.english: 68:13 They that sat in the gate spoke against me: * and they that drank wine made me their song.

segments.t: Advérsum me loquebántur, qui sedébant in porta: * et in me psallébant qui bibébant vinum.

content.latin: 68:13 Ego vero oratiónem meam ad te, Dómine: * tempus benepláciti, Deus.
content.english: 68:13 But as for me, my prayer is to thee, O Lord; * for the time of thy good pleasure, O God.

segments.t: Ego vero oratiónem meam ad te, Dómine: * tempus benepláciti, Deus.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Salvum me fac, Deus, quóniam intravérunt aquæ usque ad ánimam meam.
content.english: Ant. Save me, O God for the waters are come in even unto my soul.

segments.t: Ant.
Salvum me fac, Deus, quóniam intravérunt aquæ usque ad ánimam meam.

content.latin: Ant. Propter inimícos meos * éripe me, Dómine.
content.english: Ant. O Lord, save me * from my enemies.

segments.t: Ant.
Propter inimícos meos * éripe me, Dómine.
Psalmus 68(14-29)

content.latin: 68:14 In multitúdine misericórdiæ tuæ exáudi me, * in veritáte salútis tuæ:
content.english: 68:14 In the multitude of thy mercy hear me, * in the truth of thy salvation.

segments.t: In multitúdine misericórdiæ tuæ exáudi me, * in veritáte salútis tuæ:

content.latin: 68:15 Éripe me de luto, ut non infígar: * líbera me ab iis, qui odérunt me, et de profúndis aquárum.
content.english: 68:15 Draw me out of the mire, that I may not stick fast: * deliver me from them that hate me, and out of the deep waters.

segments.t: Éripe me de luto, ut non infígar: * líbera me ab iis, qui odérunt me, et de profúndis aquárum.

content.latin: 68:16 Non me demérgat tempéstas aquæ, neque absórbeat me profúndum: * neque úrgeat super me púteus os suum.
content.english: 68:16 Let not the tempest of water drown me, nor the deep swallow me up: * and let not the pit shut her mouth upon me.

segments.t: Non me demérgat tempéstas aquæ, neque absórbeat me profúndum: * neque úrgeat super me púteus os suum.

content.latin: 68:17 Exáudi me, Dómine, quóniam benígna est misericórdia tua: * secúndum multitúdinem miseratiónum tuárum réspice in me.
content.english: 68:17 Hear me, O Lord, for thy mercy is kind; * look upon me according to the multitude of thy tender mercies.

segments.t: Exáudi me, Dómine, quóniam benígna est misericórdia tua: * secúndum multitúdinem miseratiónum tuárum réspice in me.

content.latin: 68:18 Et ne avértas fáciem tuam a púero tuo: * quóniam tríbulor, velóciter exáudi me.
content.english: 68:18 And turn not away thy face from thy servant: * for I am in trouble, hear me speedily.

segments.t: Et ne avértas fáciem tuam a púero tuo: * quóniam tríbulor, velóciter exáudi me.

content.latin: 68:19 Inténde ánimæ meæ, et líbera eam: * propter inimícos meos éripe me.
content.english: 68:19 Attend to my soul, and deliver it: * save me because of my enemies.

segments.t: Inténde ánimæ meæ, et líbera eam: * propter inimícos meos éripe me.

content.latin: 68:20 Tu scis impropérium meum, et confusiónem meam, * et reveréntiam meam.
content.english: 68:20 Thou knowest my reproach, and my confusion, * and my shame.

segments.t: Tu scis impropérium meum, et confusiónem meam, * et reveréntiam meam.

content.latin: 68:21 In conspéctu tuo sunt omnes qui tríbulant me: * impropérium exspectávit cor meum, et misériam.
content.english: 68:21 In thy sight are all they that afflict me; * my heart hath expected reproach and misery.

segments.t: In conspéctu tuo sunt omnes qui tríbulant me: * impropérium exspectávit cor meum, et misériam.

content.latin: 68:21 Et sustínui qui simul contristarétur, et non fuit: * et qui consolarétur, et non invéni.
content.english: 68:21 And I looked for one that would grieve together with me, * but there was none: and for one that would comfort me, and I found none.

segments.t: Et sustínui qui simul contristarétur, et non fuit: * et qui consolarétur, et non invéni.

content.latin: 68:22 Et dedérunt in escam meam fel: * et in siti mea potavérunt me acéto.
content.english: 68:22 And they gave me gall for my food, * and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.

segments.t: Et dedérunt in escam meam fel: * et in siti mea potavérunt me acéto.

content.latin: 68:23 Fiat mensa eórum coram ipsis in láqueum, * et in retributiónes, et in scándalum.
content.english: 68:23 Let their table become as a snare before them, * and a recompense, and a stumblingblock.

segments.t: Fiat mensa eórum coram ipsis in láqueum, * et in retributiónes, et in scándalum.

content.latin: 68:24 Obscuréntur óculi eórum ne vídeant: * et dorsum eórum semper incúrva.
content.english: 68:24 Let their eyes be darkened that they see not; * and their back bend thou down always.

segments.t: Obscuréntur óculi eórum ne vídeant: * et dorsum eórum semper incúrva.

content.latin: 68:25 Effúnde super eos iram tuam: * et furor iræ tuæ comprehéndat eos.
content.english: 68:25 Pour out thy indignation upon them: * and let thy wrathful anger take hold of them.

segments.t: Effúnde super eos iram tuam: * et furor iræ tuæ comprehéndat eos.

content.latin: 68:26 Fiat habitátio eórum desérta: * et in tabernáculis eórum non sit qui inhábitet.
content.english: 68:26 Let their habitation be made desolate: * and let there be none to dwell in their tabernacles.

segments.t: Fiat habitátio eórum desérta: * et in tabernáculis eórum non sit qui inhábitet.

content.latin: 68:27 Quóniam quem tu percussísti, persecúti sunt: * et super dolórem vúlnerum meórum addidérunt.
content.english: 68:27 Because they have persecuted him whom thou hast smitten; * and they have added to the grief of my wounds.

segments.t: Quóniam quem tu percussísti, persecúti sunt: * et super dolórem vúlnerum meórum addidérunt.

content.latin: 68:28 Appóne iniquitátem super iniquitátem eórum: * et non intrent in iustítiam tuam.
content.english: 68:28 Add thou iniquity upon their iniquity: * and let them not come into thy justice.

segments.t: Appóne iniquitátem super iniquitátem eórum: * et non intrent in iustítiam tuam.

content.latin: 68:29 Deleántur de libro vivéntium: * et cum iustis non scribántur.
content.english: 68:29 Let them be blotted out of the book of the living; * and with the just let them not be written.

segments.t: Deleántur de libro vivéntium: * et cum iustis non scribántur.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Propter inimícos meos éripe me, Dómine.
content.english: Ant. O Lord, save me from my enemies.

segments.t: Ant.
Propter inimícos meos éripe me, Dómine.

content.latin: Ant. Quǽrite Dóminum, * et vivet ánima vestra.
content.english: Ant. Look for the Lord * and your soul shall live.

segments.t: Ant.
Quǽrite Dóminum, * et vivet ánima vestra.
Psalmus 68(30-37)

content.latin: 68:30 Ego sum pauper et dolens: * salus tua, Deus, suscépit me.
content.english: 68:30 I am poor and sorrowful: * thy salvation, O God, hath set me up.

segments.t: Ego sum pauper et dolens: * salus tua, Deus, suscépit me.

content.latin: 68:31 Laudábo nomen Dei cum cántico: * et magnificábo eum in laude:
content.english: 68:31 I will praise the name of God with a canticle: * and I will magnify him with praise.

segments.t: Laudábo nomen Dei cum cántico: * et magnificábo eum in laude:

content.latin: 68:32 Et placébit Deo super vítulum novéllum: * córnua producéntem et úngulas.
content.english: 68:32 And it shall please God better than a young calf, * that bringeth forth horns and hoofs.

segments.t: Et placébit Deo super vítulum novéllum: * córnua producéntem et úngulas.

content.latin: 68:33 Vídeant páuperes et læténtur: * quǽrite Deum, et vivet ánima vestra.
content.english: 68:33 Let the poor see and rejoice: * seek ye God, and your soul shall live.

segments.t: Vídeant páuperes et læténtur: * quǽrite Deum, et vivet ánima vestra.

content.latin: 68:34 Quóniam exaudívit páuperes Dóminus: * et vinctos suos non despéxit.
content.english: 68:34 For the Lord hath heard the poor: * and hath not despised his prisoners.

segments.t: Quóniam exaudívit páuperes Dóminus: * et vinctos suos non despéxit.

content.latin: 68:35 Laudent illum cæli et terra, * mare et ómnia reptília in eis.
content.english: 68:35 Let the heavens and the earth praise him; * the sea, and every thing that creepeth therein.

segments.t: Laudent illum cæli et terra, * mare et ómnia reptília in eis.

content.latin: 68:36 Quóniam Deus salvam fáciet Sion: * et ædificabúntur civitátes Iuda.
content.english: 68:36 For God will save Sion, * and the cities of Juda shall be built up.

segments.t: Quóniam Deus salvam fáciet Sion: * et ædificabúntur civitátes Iuda.

content.latin: 68:36 Et inhabitábunt ibi, * et hereditáte acquírent eam.
content.english: 68:36 And they shall dwell there, * and acquire it by inheritance.

segments.t: Et inhabitábunt ibi, * et hereditáte acquírent eam.

content.latin: 68:37 Et semen servórum eius possidébit eam: * et qui díligunt nomen eius, habitábunt in ea.
content.english: 68:37 And the seed of his servants shall possess it; * and they that love his name shall dwell therein.

segments.t: Et semen servórum eius possidébit eam: * et qui díligunt nomen eius, habitábunt in ea.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Quǽrite Dóminum, et vivet ánima vestra.
content.english: Ant. Look for the Lord and your soul shall live.

segments.t: Ant.
Quǽrite Dóminum, et vivet ánima vestra.

content.latin: ℣. Laudábo nomen Dei cum cántico.
content.english: ℣. I will praise the name of God.

segments.t: Laudábo nomen Dei cum cántico.

content.latin: ℟. Et magnificábo eum in laude.
content.english: ℟. And I will magnify him with praise.

segments.t: Et magnificábo eum in laude.

content.latin: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

segments.t: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: ℣. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

segments.t: Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: ℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.
content.english: ℟. But deliver us from evil.

segments.t: Sed líbera nos a malo.

content.latin: Absolutio. Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Absolution. O Lord Jesus Christ, graciously hear the prayers of Thy servants, and have mercy upon us, Who livest and reignest with the Father, and the Holy Ghost, ever world without end.

segments.t: Absolutio.
Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.

content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Ille nos benedícat, qui sine fine vivit et regnat.
content.english: Benediction. May His blessing be upon us who doth live and reign for ever.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Ille nos benedícat, qui sine fine vivit et regnat.

content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: De Daniéle Prophéta
content.english: Lesson from the book of Daniel

content.latin: 1 Baltássar rex fecit grande convívium optimátibus suis mille: et unusquísque secúndum suam bibébat ætátem.
content.english: 1 Baltasar the king made a great feast for a thousand of his nobles: and every one drank according to his age.

segments.t: Baltássar rex fecit grande convívium optimátibus suis mille: et unusquísque secúndum suam bibébat ætátem.

content.latin: 2 Præcépit ergo iam temuléntus ut afferréntur vasa áurea et argéntea, quæ asportáverat Nabuchodónosor pater eius de templo, quod fuit in Ierúsalem, ut bíberent in eis rex, et optimátes eius, uxorésque eius, et concubínæ.
content.english: 2 And being now drunk he commanded that they should bring the vessels of gold and silver which Nabuchodonosor his father had brought away out of the temple, that was in Jerusalem, that the king and his nobles, and his wives and his concubines, might drink in them.

segments.t: Præcépit ergo iam temuléntus ut afferréntur vasa áurea et argéntea, quæ asportáverat Nabuchodónosor pater eius de templo, quod fuit in Ierúsalem, ut bíberent in eis rex, et optimátes eius, uxorésque eius, et concubínæ.

content.latin: 3 Tunc alláta sunt vasa áurea, et argéntea, quæ asportáverat de templo, quod fúerat in Ierúsalem: et bibérunt in eis rex, et optimátes eius, uxóres et concubínæ illíus.
content.english: 3 Then were the golden and silver vessels brought, which he had brought away out of the temple that was in Jerusalem: and the king and his nobles, his wives and his concubines, drank in them.

segments.t: Tunc alláta sunt vasa áurea, et argéntea, quæ asportáverat de templo, quod fúerat in Ierúsalem: et bibérunt in eis rex, et optimátes eius, uxóres et concubínæ illíus.

content.latin: 4 Bibébant vinum, et laudábant deos suos áureos et argénteos, ǽreos, férreos, ligneósque et lapídeos.
content.english: 4 They drank wine, and praised their gods of gold, and of silver, of brass, of iron, and of wood, and of stone.

segments.t: Bibébant vinum, et laudábant deos suos áureos et argénteos, ǽreos, férreos, ligneósque et lapídeos.

content.latin: 5 In eádem hora apparuérunt dígiti, quasi manus hóminis scribéntis contra candelábrum in superfície paríetis aulæ régiæ: et rex aspiciébat artículos manus scribéntis.
content.english: 5 In the same hour there appeared fingers, as it were of the hand of a man, writing over against the candlestick upon the surface of the wall of the king's palace: and the king beheld the joints of the hand that wrote.

segments.t: In eádem hora apparuérunt dígiti, quasi manus hóminis scribéntis contra candelábrum in superfície paríetis aulæ régiæ: et rex aspiciébat artículos manus scribéntis.

content.latin: 6 Tunc fácies regis commutáta est, et cogitatiónes eius conturbábant eum: et compáges renum eius solvebántur, et génua eius ad se ínvicem collidebántur.
content.english: 6 Then was the king's countenance changed, and his thoughts troubled him.

segments.t: Tunc fácies regis commutáta est, et cogitatiónes eius conturbábant eum: et compáges renum eius solvebántur, et génua eius ad se ínvicem collidebántur.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Vidi Dóminum sedéntem super sólium excélsum et elevátum, et plena erat omnis terra maiestáte eius:
content.english: ℟. I saw the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and the whole earth was full of His glory;

segments.t: Vidi Dóminum sedéntem super sólium excélsum et elevátum, et plena erat omnis terra maiestáte eius:

content.latin: * Et ea, quæ sub ipso erant, replébant templum.
content.english: * And His train filled the temple.

content.latin: ℣. Séraphim stabant super illud: sex alæ uni, et sex alæ álteri.
content.english: ℣. Above it stood the Seraphim each one had six wings.

segments.t: Séraphim stabant super illud: sex alæ uni, et sex alæ álteri.

content.latin: ℟. Et ea, quæ sub ipso erant, replébant templum.
content.english: ℟. And His train filled the temple.

segments.t: Et ea, quæ sub ipso erant, replébant templum.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Cuius festum cólimus, ipse intercédat pro nobis ad Dóminum.
content.english: Benediction. He whose feast-day we are keeping, be our Advocate with God.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Cuius festum cólimus, ipse intercédat pro nobis ad Dóminum.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: 13 Igitur introdúctus est Dániel coram rege: ad quem præfátus rex ait: Tu es Dániel de fíliis captivitátis Iudæ, quem addúxit pater meus rex de Iudǽa?
content.english: 13 Then Daniel was brought in before the king. And the king spoke, and said to him: Art thou Daniel of the children of the captivity of Juda, whom my father the king brought out of Judea?

segments.t: Igitur introdúctus est Dániel coram rege: ad quem præfátus rex ait: Tu es Dániel de fíliis captivitátis Iudæ, quem addúxit pater meus rex de Iudǽa?

content.latin: 14 Audívi de te, quóniam spíritum deórum hábeas, et sciéntia, intellegentiáque ac sapiéntia amplióres invéntæ sunt in te.
content.english: 14 I have heard of thee, that thou hast the spirit of the gods, and excellent knowledge, and understanding, and wisdom are found in thee.

segments.t: Audívi de te, quóniam spíritum deórum hábeas, et sciéntia, intellegentiáque ac sapiéntia amplióres invéntæ sunt in te.

content.latin: 15 Et nunc introgréssi sunt in conspéctu meo sapiéntes magi, ut scriptúram hanc légerent, et interpretatiónem eius indicárent mihi: et nequivérunt sensum huius sermónis edícere.
content.english: 15 And now the wise men the magicians have come in before me, to read this writing, and shew me the interpretation thereof: and they could not declare to me the meaning of this writing.

segments.t: Et nunc introgréssi sunt in conspéctu meo sapiéntes magi, ut scriptúram hanc légerent, et interpretatiónem eius indicárent mihi: et nequivérunt sensum huius sermónis edícere.

content.latin: 16 Porro ego audívi de te, quod possis obscúra interpretári, et ligáta dissólvere: si ergo vales scriptúram légere, et interpretatiónem eius indicáre mihi, púrpura vestiéris, et torquem áuream circa collum tuum habébis, et tértius in regno meo princeps eris.
content.english: 16 But I have heard of thee, that thou canst interpret obscure things, and resolve difficult things: now if thou art able to read the writing, and to shew me the interpretation thereof, thou shalt be clothed with purple, and shalt have a chain of gold about thy neck, and shalt be the third prince in my kingdom.

segments.t: Porro ego audívi de te, quod possis obscúra interpretári, et ligáta dissólvere: si ergo vales scriptúram légere, et interpretatiónem eius indicáre mihi, púrpura vestiéris, et torquem áuream circa collum tuum habébis, et tértius in regno meo princeps eris.

content.latin: 17 Ad quæ respóndens Dániel, ait coram rege: Múnera tua sint tibi, et dona domus tuæ álteri da: scriptúram autem legam tibi, rex, et interpretatiónem eius osténdam tibi.
content.english: 17 To which Daniel made answer, and said before the king: thy rewards be to thyself, and the gifts of thy house give to another: but the writing I will read to thee, O king, and shew thee the interpretation thereof.

segments.t: Ad quæ respóndens Dániel, ait coram rege: Múnera tua sint tibi, et dona domus tuæ álteri da: scriptúram autem legam tibi, rex, et interpretatiónem eius osténdam tibi.

content.latin: 25 Hæc est autem scriptúra, quæ digésta est: Mane, Thecel, Phares.
content.english: 25 And this is the writing that is written: MANE, THECEL, PHARES.

segments.t: Hæc est autem scriptúra, quæ digésta est: Mane, Thecel, Phares.

content.latin: 26 Et hæc est interpretátio sermónis. Mane: numerávit Deus regnum tuum, et complévit illud.
content.english: 26 And this is the interpretation of the word. MANE: God hath numbered thy kingdom, and hath finished it.

segments.t: Et hæc est interpretátio sermónis. Mane: numerávit Deus regnum tuum, et complévit illud.

content.latin: 27 Thecel: appénsus es in statéra, et invéntus es minus habens.
content.english: 27 THECEL: thou art weighed in the balance, and art found wanting.

segments.t: Thecel: appénsus es in statéra, et invéntus es minus habens.

content.latin: 28 Phares: divísum est regnum tuum, et datum est Medis, et Persis.
content.english: 28 PHARES: thy kingdom is divided, and is given to the Medes and Persians.

segments.t: Phares: divísum est regnum tuum, et datum est Medis, et Persis.

content.latin: 29 Tunc, iubénte rege, indútus est Dániel púrpura, et circúmdata est torques áurea collo eius: et prædicátum est de eo quod habéret potestátem tértius in regno suo.
content.english: 29 Then by the king's command Daniel was clothed with purple, and a chain of gold was put about his neck: and it was proclaimed of him that he had power as the third man in the kingdom.

segments.t: Tunc, iubénte rege, indútus est Dániel púrpura, et circúmdata est torques áurea collo eius: et prædicátum est de eo quod habéret potestátem tértius in regno suo.

content.latin: 30 Eádem nocte interféctus est Baltássar rex Chaldǽus.
content.english: 30 The same night Baltasar the Chaldean king was slain.

segments.t: Eádem nocte interféctus est Baltássar rex Chaldǽus.

content.latin: 31 Et Daríus Medus succéssit in regnum, annos natus sexagínta duos.
content.english: 31 And Darius the Mede succeeded to the kingdom, being threescore and two years old.

segments.t: Et Daríus Medus succéssit in regnum, annos natus sexagínta duos.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Aspice, Dómine, quia facta est desoláta cívitas plena divítiis, sedet in tristítia dómina géntium:
content.english: ℟. Consider, O Lord, how that the city sitteth solitary that was full of riches; how is she become as a widow, she that was great among the nations;

segments.t: Aspice, Dómine, quia facta est desoláta cívitas plena divítiis, sedet in tristítia dómina géntium:

content.latin: * Non est qui consolétur eam, nisi tu, Deus noster.
content.english: * She hath none to comfort her, save thee, O our God.

content.latin: ℣. Plorans plorávit in nocte, et lácrimæ eius in maxíllis eius.

content.latin: Martínus, Tudérti in Umbria natus, inítio pontificátus, et lítteris et legatiónibus missis óperam dedit, ut ad cathólicam veritátem revocáret Paulum Constantinopolitánum hæréticum, qui, Constánte imperatóre fretus, vel ipsos apostólicæ Sedis legátos várias in ínsulas relegáverat. Hoc scélere commótus Póntifex, coácto Romæ concílio centum quinque episcopórum, eum condemnávit. Quo duránte concílio, imperátor in Itáliam Olýmpium exárchum misit, qui summum Pontíficem extrúderet. Verum cum Olýmpius nullum Martíno malum inférre potuísset, et mox misérrime decessísset; Theodórus Callíopas, iussu imperatóris, basílica Lateranénsi proximísque pontificálibus ǽdibus occupátis, Martínum vi captum primo in ínsulam Naxum relegávit, dein Constantinópolim perdúxit. Ibi sanctus Póntifex, in víncula coniéctus, ludíbria et contumélias expértus est, donec pulsus in Chersonésum, ob cathólicam fidem ærúmnis et inópia conféctus, cessit e vita, pontificátus sui anno octávo incépto. Eius corpus, Romam póstea translátum, in ecclésia cónditum est, quæ sanctórum Silvéstri et Martíni nómine dedicáta est.
content.english: Born at Todi in Umbria, Martin accepted at the beginning of his pontificate to recall Paul of Constantinople, a heretic to the Catholic faith, by sending letters and legates. But Paul, supported by the emperor Constans, banished the legates of the Apostolic See to various islands. The Pope aroused by this crime, gathered at Rome a council of one hundred and five bishops, who condemned Paul. During the council the emperor sent the exarch Olympius to Italy, to depose the Pope. But Olympius died a miserable death, after failing to harm Martin in any way. Then, on the emperor’s orders, Theodore Kalliopes took over the Lateran Basilica and the nearby residence of the pope, and arrested Martin, first sending him to the island of Naxos, and then bringing him to Constantinople. Here the holy pope was chained and suffered mockery and insults. Exiled to the Chersonesus, he departed his life in the beginning of the eighth year of his pontificate, worn out with hardship and destitution for the sake of the Catholic faith. His body was later taken to Rome and was buried in the Church dedicated to SS. Sylvester and Martin.

content.latin: 35:2 Dixit iniústus ut delínquat in semetípso: * non est timor Dei ante óculos eius.
content.english: 35:2 The unjust hath said within himself, that he would sin: * there is no fear of God before his eyes.

segments.t: Dixit iniústus ut delínquat in semetípso: * non est timor Dei ante óculos eius.

content.latin: 35:3 Quóniam dolóse egit in conspéctu eius: * ut inveniátur iníquitas eius ad ódium.
content.english: 35:3 For in his sight he hath done deceitfully, * that his iniquity may be found unto hatred.

segments.t: Quóniam dolóse egit in conspéctu eius: * ut inveniátur iníquitas eius ad ódium.

content.latin: 35:4 Verba oris eius iníquitas, et dolus: * nóluit intellégere ut bene ágeret.
content.english: 35:4 The words of his mouth are iniquity and guile: * he would not understand that he might do well.

segments.t: Verba oris eius iníquitas, et dolus: * nóluit intellégere ut bene ágeret.

content.latin: 35:5 Iniquitátem meditátus est in cubíli suo: * ástitit omni viæ non bonæ, malítiam autem non odívit.
content.english: 35:5 He hath devised iniquity on his bed, * he hath set himself on every way that is not good: but evil he hath not hated.

segments.t: Iniquitátem meditátus est in cubíli suo: * ástitit omni viæ non bonæ, malítiam autem non odívit.

content.latin: 35:6 Dómine, in cælo misericórdia tua: * et véritas tua usque ad nubes.
content.english: 35:6 O Lord, thy mercy is in heaven, * and thy truth reacheth even to the clouds.

segments.t: Dómine, in cælo misericórdia tua: * et véritas tua usque ad nubes.

content.latin: 35:7 Iustítia tua sicut montes Dei: * iudícia tua abýssus multa.
content.english: 35:7 Thy justice is as the mountains of God, * thy judgments are a great deep.

segments.t: Iustítia tua sicut montes Dei: * iudícia tua abýssus multa.

content.latin: 35:7 Hómines, et iuménta salvábis, Dómine: * quemádmodum multiplicásti misericórdiam tuam, Deus.
content.english: 35:7 Men and beasts thou wilt preserve, O Lord: * O how hast thou multiplied thy mercy, O God!

segments.t: Hómines, et iuménta salvábis, Dómine: * quemádmodum multiplicásti misericórdiam tuam, Deus.

content.latin: 35:8 Fílii autem hóminum, * in tégmine alárum tuárum sperábunt.
content.english: 35:8 But the children of men * shall put their trust under the covert of thy wings.

segments.t: Fílii autem hóminum, * in tégmine alárum tuárum sperábunt.

content.latin: 35:9 Inebriabúntur ab ubertáte domus tuæ: * et torrénte voluptátis tuæ potábis eos.
content.english: 35:9 They shall be inebriated with the plenty of thy house; * and thou shalt make them drink of the torrent of thy pleasure.

segments.t: Inebriabúntur ab ubertáte domus tuæ: * et torrénte voluptátis tuæ potábis eos.

content.latin: 35:10 Quóniam apud te est fons vitæ: * et in lúmine tuo vidébimus lumen.
content.english: 35:10 For with thee is the fountain of life; * and in thy light we shall see light.

segments.t: Quóniam apud te est fons vitæ: * et in lúmine tuo vidébimus lumen.

content.latin: 35:11 Præténde misericórdiam tuam sciéntibus te, * et iustítiam tuam his, qui recto sunt corde.
content.english: 35:11 Extend thy mercy to them that know thee, * and thy justice to them that are right in heart.

segments.t: Præténde misericórdiam tuam sciéntibus te, * et iustítiam tuam his, qui recto sunt corde.

content.latin: 35:12 Non véniat mihi pes supérbiæ: * et manus peccatóris non móveat me.
content.english: 35:12 Let not the foot of pride come to me, * and let not the hand of the sinner move me.

segments.t: Non véniat mihi pes supérbiæ: * et manus peccatóris non móveat me.

content.latin: 35:13 Ibi cecidérunt qui operántur iniquitátem: * expúlsi sunt, nec potuérunt stare.
content.english: 35:13 There the workers of iniquity are fallen, * they are cast out, and could not stand.

segments.t: Ibi cecidérunt qui operántur iniquitátem: * expúlsi sunt, nec potuérunt stare.

content.english: 31:10 Hear the word of the Lord, O ye nations, * and declare it in the islands that are afar off,

segments.t: Audíte verbum Dómini, gentes, * et annuntiáte in ínsulis, quæ procul sunt,

content.latin: 31:11 Et dícite: Qui dispérsit Israël, congregábit eum: * et custódiet eum sicut pastor gregem suum.
content.english: 31:11 And say: He that scattered Israel will gather him: * and he will keep him as the shepherd doth his flock.

segments.t: Et dícite: Qui dispérsit Israël, congregábit eum: * et custódiet eum sicut pastor gregem suum.

content.latin: 31:12 Redémit enim Dóminus Iacob, * et liberávit eum de manu potentióris.
content.english: 31:12 For the Lord hath redeemed Jacob, * and delivered him out of the hand of one that was mightier than he.

segments.t: Redémit enim Dóminus Iacob, * et liberávit eum de manu potentióris.

content.latin: 31:13 Et vénient, et laudábunt in monte Sion: * et cónfluent ad bona Dómini,
content.english: 31:13 And they shall come, and shall give praise in mount Sion: * and they shall flow together to the good things of the Lord,

segments.t: Et vénient, et laudábunt in monte Sion: * et cónfluent ad bona Dómini,

content.latin: 31:14 Super fruménto, et vino, et óleo, * et fœtu pécorum et armentórum:
content.english: 31:14 For the corn, and wine, and oil, * and the increase of cattle and herds,

segments.t: Super fruménto, et vino, et óleo, * et fœtu pécorum et armentórum:

content.latin: 31:15 Erítque ánima eórum quasi hortus irríguus, * et ultra non esúrient.
content.english: 31:15 And their soul shall be as a watered garden, * and they shall be hungry no more.

segments.t: Erítque ánima eórum quasi hortus irríguus, * et ultra non esúrient.

content.latin: 31:16 Tunc lætábitur virgo in choro, * iúvenes et senes simul:
content.english: 31:16 Then shall the virgin rejoice in the dance, * the young men and old men together:

segments.t: Tunc lætábitur virgo in choro, * iúvenes et senes simul:

content.latin: 31:17 Et convértam luctum eórum in gáudium, * et consolábor eos, et lætificábo a dolóre suo.
content.english: 31:17 And I will turn their mourning into joy, * and will comfort them, and make them joyful after their sorrow.

segments.t: Et convértam luctum eórum in gáudium, * et consolábor eos, et lætificábo a dolóre suo.

content.latin: 31:18 Et inebriábo ánimam sacerdótum pinguédine: * et pópulus meus bonis meis adimplébitur.
content.english: 31:18 And I will fill the soul of the priests with fatness: * and my people shall be filled with my good things.

segments.t: Et inebriábo ánimam sacerdótum pinguédine: * et pópulus meus bonis meis adimplébitur.

content.latin: 146:1 Laudáte Dóminum quóniam bonus est psalmus: * Deo nostro sit iucúnda, decóraque laudátio.
content.english: 146:1 Praise ye the Lord, because psalm is good: * to our God be joyful and comely praise.

segments.t: Laudáte Dóminum quóniam bonus est psalmus: * Deo nostro sit iucúnda, decóraque laudátio.

content.latin: 146:2 Ædíficans Ierúsalem Dóminus: * dispersiónes Israélis congregábit.
content.english: 146:2 The Lord buildeth up Jerusalem: * he will gather together the dispersed of Israel

segments.t: Ædíficans Ierúsalem Dóminus: * dispersiónes Israélis congregábit.

content.latin: 146:3 Qui sanat contrítos corde: * et álligat contritiónes eórum.
content.english: 146:3 Who healeth the broken of heart, * and bindeth up their bruises.

segments.t: Qui sanat contrítos corde: * et álligat contritiónes eórum.

content.latin: 146:4 Qui númerat multitúdinem stellárum: * et ómnibus eis nómina vocat.
content.english: 146:4 Who telleth the number of the stars: * and calleth them all by their names.

segments.t: Qui númerat multitúdinem stellárum: * et ómnibus eis nómina vocat.

content.latin: 146:5 Magnus Dóminus noster, et magna virtus eius: * et sapiéntiæ eius non est númerus.
content.english: 146:5 Great is our Lord, and great is his power: * and of his wisdom there is no number.

segments.t: Magnus Dóminus noster, et magna virtus eius: * et sapiéntiæ eius non est númerus.

content.latin: 146:6 Suscípiens mansuétos Dóminus: * humílians autem peccatóres usque ad terram.
content.english: 146:6 The Lord lifteth up the meek, * and bringeth the wicked down even to the ground.

segments.t: Suscípiens mansuétos Dóminus: * humílians autem peccatóres usque ad terram.

content.latin: 146:7 Præcínite Dómino in confessióne: * psállite Deo nostro in cíthara.
content.english: 146:7 Sing ye to the Lord with praise: * sing to our God upon the harp.

segments.t: Præcínite Dómino in confessióne: * psállite Deo nostro in cíthara.

content.latin: 146:8 Qui óperit cælum núbibus: * et parat terræ plúviam.
content.english: 146:8 Who covereth the heaven with clouds, * and prepareth rain for the earth.

segments.t: Qui óperit cælum núbibus: * et parat terræ plúviam.

content.latin: 146:8 Qui prodúcit in móntibus fænum: * et herbam servitúti hóminum.
content.english: 146:8 Who maketh grass to grow on the mountains, * and herbs for the service of men.

segments.t: Qui prodúcit in móntibus fænum: * et herbam servitúti hóminum.

content.latin: 146:9 Qui dat iuméntis escam ipsórum: * et pullis corvórum invocántibus eum.
content.english: 146:9 Who giveth to beasts their food: * and to the young ravens that call upon him.

segments.t: Qui dat iuméntis escam ipsórum: * et pullis corvórum invocántibus eum.

content.latin: 146:10 Non in fortitúdine equi voluntátem habébit: * nec in tíbiis viri beneplácitum erit ei.
content.english: 146:10 He shall not delight in the strength of the horse: * nor take pleasure in the legs of a man.

segments.t: Non in fortitúdine equi voluntátem habébit: * nec in tíbiis viri beneplácitum erit ei.

content.latin: 146:11 Beneplácitum est Dómino super timéntes eum: * et in eis, qui sperant super misericórdia eius.
content.english: 146:11 The Lord taketh pleasure in them that fear him: * and in them that hope in his mercy.

segments.t: Beneplácitum est Dómino super timéntes eum: * et in eis, qui sperant super misericórdia eius.

content.english: And well thy heavenly bliss was won!

content.english: Long, long ago, were loosed the chains

content.english: All praise, O Holy Ghost, to thee,

content.english: While never-ending ages run.

content.latin: 1:68 Benedíctus ✠ Dóminus, Deus Israël: * quia visitávit, et fecit redemptiónem plebis suæ:
content.english: 1:68 Blessed be the Lord ✠ God of Israel; * because he hath visited and wrought the redemption of his people:

segments.t: Benedíctus ✠ Dóminus, Deus Israël: * quia visitávit, et fecit redemptiónem plebis suæ:

content.latin: 1:69 Et eréxit cornu salútis nobis: * in domo David, púeri sui.
content.english: 1:69 And hath raised up an horn of salvation to us, * in the house of David his servant:

segments.t: Et eréxit cornu salútis nobis: * in domo David, púeri sui.

content.latin: 1:70 Sicut locútus est per os sanctórum, * qui a sǽculo sunt, prophetárum eius:
content.english: 1:70 As he spoke by the mouth of his holy Prophets, * who are from the beginning:

segments.t: Sicut locútus est per os sanctórum, * qui a sǽculo sunt, prophetárum eius:

content.latin: 1:71 Salútem ex inimícis nostris, * et de manu ómnium, qui odérunt nos.
content.english: 1:71 Salvation from our enemies, * and from the hand of all that hate us:

segments.t: Salútem ex inimícis nostris, * et de manu ómnium, qui odérunt nos.

content.latin: 1:72 Ad faciéndam misericórdiam cum pátribus nostris: * et memorári testaménti sui sancti.
content.english: 1:72 To perform mercy to our fathers, * and to remember his holy testament,

segments.t: Ad faciéndam misericórdiam cum pátribus nostris: * et memorári testaménti sui sancti.

content.latin: 1:73 Iusiurándum, quod iurávit ad Ábraham patrem nostrum, * datúrum se nobis:
content.english: 1:73 The oath, which he swore to Abraham our father, * that he would grant to us,

segments.t: Iusiurándum, quod iurávit ad Ábraham patrem nostrum, * datúrum se nobis:

content.latin: 1:74 Ut sine timóre, de manu inimicórum nostrórum liberáti, * serviámus illi.
content.english: 1:74 That being delivered from the hand of our enemies, * we may serve him without fear,

segments.t: Ut sine timóre, de manu inimicórum nostrórum liberáti, * serviámus illi.

content.latin: 1:75 In sanctitáte, et iustítia coram ipso, * ómnibus diébus nostris.
content.english: 1:75 In holiness and justice before him, * all our days.

segments.t: In sanctitáte, et iustítia coram ipso, * ómnibus diébus nostris.

content.latin: 1:76 Et tu, puer, Prophéta Altíssimi vocáberis: * præíbis enim ante fáciem Dómini, paráre vias eius:
content.english: 1:76 And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest: * for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways:

segments.t: Et tu, puer, Prophéta Altíssimi vocáberis: * præíbis enim ante fáciem Dómini, paráre vias eius:

content.latin: 1:77 Ad dandam sciéntiam salútis plebi eius: * in remissiónem peccatórum eórum:
content.english: 1:77 To give knowledge of salvation to his people, * unto the remission of their sins:

segments.t: Ad dandam sciéntiam salútis plebi eius: * in remissiónem peccatórum eórum:

content.latin: 1:78 Per víscera misericórdiæ Dei nostri: * in quibus visitávit nos, óriens ex alto:
content.english: 1:78 Through the bowels of the mercy of our God, * in which the Orient from on high hath visited us:

segments.t: Per víscera misericórdiæ Dei nostri: * in quibus visitávit nos, óriens ex alto:

content.latin: 1:79 Illumináre his, qui in ténebris, et in umbra mortis sedent: * ad dirigéndos pedes nostros in viam pacis.
content.english: 1:79 To enlighten them that sit in darkness, and in the shadow of death: * to direct our feet into the way of peace.

content.latin: Idibus Novémbris Luna tértia Anno Dómini 2026
content.english: Upon the morrow we keep the feast of the holy Confessor Diego, of the Order of Friars Minor, who was born into the better life upon this present day.

content.latin: Sancti Dídaci, ex Ordine Minórum, Confessóris; cuius dies natális recólitur prídie huius diéi.
content.english: November 13th 2026, the 3rd day of the Moon, were born into the better life:

content.latin: Ravénnæ natális sanctórum Mártyrum Valentíni, Solutóris et Victóris; qui sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre passi sunt.
content.english: At Ravenna, the holy martyrs Valentine, Solutor, and Victor, who suffered in the persecution under Diocletian.

content.latin: Aquis, in província Narbonénsi, beáti Mítrii, claríssimi Mártyris.
content.english: At Aix, in Provence, (in the year 304,) that illustrious martyr the blessed Mitrius.

content.latin: Cæsaréæ, in Palæstína, pássio sanctórum Antoníni, Zébinæ, Germáni et Ennathæ Vírginis. Hæc, sub Galério Maximiáno Imperatóre, verbéribus cæsa, igne cremáta est; illi vero, cum intrépidi ac líbera voce Firmiliánum Prǽsidem, diis immolántem, impietátis argúerent, cápite cæsi sunt.
content.english: At Caesarea, in Palestine, (in the year 308,) in the persecution under the Emperor Galerius Maximian, the holy martyrs Antonine, Zebinas, German, and the Virgin Ennatha. Ennatha was flogged and then burnt, and the men were beheaded because they openly rebuked the President Firmilian for his wickedness in offering sacrifice to the gods.

content.latin: In Africa sanctórum Mártyrum Hispanórum Arcádii, Paschásii, Probi et Eutychiáni; qui, in persecutióne Wandálica, cum in Ariánam perfídiam nullátenus declináre pateréntur, hinc a Genseríco, Rege Ariáno, primum proscrípti, deínde acti in exsílium atque atrocíssimis supplíciis cruciáti, postrémum divérso mortis génere interémpti sunt. Tunc et Paulílli puéruli, germáni sanctórum Paschásii et Eutychiáni, constántia enítuit; qui, cum de fide cathólica nullátenus posset avélli, fústibus diu cæsus est, atque ad ínfimam servitútem damnátus.
content.english: In Africa, (in the year 437,) the holy martyrs Arcadius, Paschasius, Probus, and Eutychian. These were all Spaniards who, during the persecution under the Vandals, could no wise be brought to turn aside unto the Arian misbelief. For this cause the Arian king Genseric first proscribed them, then banished them, afterwards tormented them with terrible sufferings, and lastly put them to death in diverse ways. Then also became glorious the faithfulness of the little lad, Paulillus, the brother of holy Paschasius and Eutychian, and as he would not give up the Catholic faith, he was cudgelled for a long time and condemned to the lowest bondage.

content.latin: Romæ sancti Nicolái Papæ Primi, vigóre apostólico præstántis.
content.english: At Rome, holy Pope Nicholas the Great, eminent for his Apostolic vigour. (He reigned from April 28, 858 to November 13, 867. He was the 107th Pope.)

content.latin: Turónis, in Gállia, sancti Brítii Epíscopi, qui fuit discípulus beáti Martíni Epíscopi.
content.english: At Tours, (in the year 444,) holy Brice, Bishop of that see, a disciple of the blessed Bishop Martin.

content.latin: Toléti, in Hispánia, sancti Eugénii Epíscopi.
content.english: At Toledo, (in the year 658,) holy Eugene, Bishop (of that see.)

content.latin: Arvérnis, in Gállia, sancti Quinctiáni Epíscopi.
content.english: In Auvergne, (in the year 527,) holy Quintian, Bishop (of Rodez and of Clermont.)

content.latin: Cremónæ, in Insúbria, sancti Homobóni Confessóris; quem, miráculis clarum, Innocéntius Papa Tértius in Sanctórum númerum rétulit.
content.english: At Cremona, the holy Confessor Homobuono, who was famous for miracles, and whose name Innocent III enrolled among those of the Saints.

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:

content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Dirígere et sanctificáre, régere et gubernáre dignáre, Dómine Deus, Rex cæli et terræ, hódie corda et córpora nostra, sensus, sermónes et actus nostros in lege tua, et in opéribus mandatórum tuórum: ut hic et in ætérnum, te auxiliánte, salvi et líberi esse mereámur, Salvátor mundi: Qui vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.

content.latin: 72:1 Quam bonus Israël Deus, his, qui recto sunt corde!
content.english: 72:1 How good is God to Israel, to them that are of a right heart!

segments.t: Quam bonus Israël Deus, his, qui recto sunt corde!

content.latin: 72:2 ‡ Mei autem pæne moti sunt pedes: * pæne effúsi sunt gressus mei.
content.english: 72:2 ‡ But my feet were almost moved; * my steps had wellnigh slipped.

segments.t: Mei autem pæne moti sunt pedes: * pæne effúsi sunt gressus mei.

content.latin: 72:3 Quia zelávi super iníquos, * pacem peccatórum videns.
content.english: 72:3 Because I had a zeal on occasion of the wicked, * seeing the prosperity of sinners.

segments.t: Quia zelávi super iníquos, * pacem peccatórum videns.

content.latin: 72:4 Quia non est respéctus morti eórum: * et firmaméntum in plaga eórum.
content.english: 72:4 For there is no regard to their death, * nor is there strength in their stripes.

segments.t: Quia non est respéctus morti eórum: * et firmaméntum in plaga eórum.

content.latin: 72:5 In labóre hóminum non sunt, * et cum homínibus non flagellabúntur:
content.english: 72:5 They are not in the labour of men: * neither shall they be scourged like other men.

segments.t: In labóre hóminum non sunt, * et cum homínibus non flagellabúntur:

content.latin: 72:6 Ídeo ténuit eos supérbia, * opérti sunt iniquitáte et impietáte sua.
content.english: 72:6 Therefore pride hath held them fast: * they are covered with their iniquity and their wickedness.

segments.t: Ídeo ténuit eos supérbia, * opérti sunt iniquitáte et impietáte sua.

content.latin: 72:7 Pródiit quasi ex ádipe iníquitas eórum: * transiérunt in afféctum cordis.
content.english: 72:7 Their iniquity hath come forth, as it were from fatness: * they have passed into the affection of the heart.

segments.t: Pródiit quasi ex ádipe iníquitas eórum: * transiérunt in afféctum cordis.

content.latin: 72:8 Cogitavérunt, et locúti sunt nequítiam: * iniquitátem in excélso locúti sunt.
content.english: 72:8 They have thought and spoken wickedness: * they have spoken iniquity on high.

segments.t: Cogitavérunt, et locúti sunt nequítiam: * iniquitátem in excélso locúti sunt.

content.latin: 72:9 Posuérunt in cælum os suum: * et lingua eórum transívit in terra.
content.english: 72:9 They have set their mouth against heaven: * and their tongue hath passed through the earth.

segments.t: Posuérunt in cælum os suum: * et lingua eórum transívit in terra.

content.english: 72:10 Therefore will my people return here * and full days shall be found in them.

segments.t: Ídeo convertétur pópulus meus hic: * et dies pleni inveniéntur in eis.

content.latin: 72:11 Et dixérunt: Quómodo scit Deus, * et si est sciéntia in excélso?
content.english: 72:11 And they said: How doth God know? * and is there knowledge in the most High?

segments.t: Et dixérunt: Quómodo scit Deus, * et si est sciéntia in excélso?

content.latin: 72:12 Ecce, ipsi peccatóres, et abundántes in sǽculo, * obtinuérunt divítias.
content.english: 72:12 Behold these are sinners; and yet abounding in the world * they have obtained riches.

segments.t: Ecce, ipsi peccatóres, et abundántes in sǽculo, * obtinuérunt divítias.

content.latin: 72:13 Et dixi: Ergo sine causa iustificávi cor meum, * et lavi inter innocéntes manus meas:
content.english: 72:13 And I said: Then have I in vain justified my heart, * and washed my hands among the innocent.

segments.t: Et dixi: Ergo sine causa iustificávi cor meum, * et lavi inter innocéntes manus meas:

content.latin: 72:14 Et fui flagellátus tota die, * et castigátio mea in matutínis.
content.english: 72:14 And I have been scourged all the day; * and my chastisement hath been in the mornings.

segments.t: Et fui flagellátus tota die, * et castigátio mea in matutínis.

content.latin: 72:15 Si dicébam: Narrábo sic: * ecce, natiónem filiórum tuórum reprobávi.
content.english: 72:15 If I said: I will speak thus; * behold I should condemn the generation of thy children.

segments.t: Si dicébam: Narrábo sic: * ecce, natiónem filiórum tuórum reprobávi.

content.latin: 72:16 Existimábam ut cognóscerem hoc, * labor est ante me:
content.english: 72:16 I studied that I might know this thing, * it is a labour in my sight:

segments.t: Existimábam ut cognóscerem hoc, * labor est ante me:

content.latin: 72:17 Donec intrem in Sanctuárium Dei: * et intéllegam in novíssimis eórum.
content.english: 72:17 Until I go into the sanctuary of God, * and understand concerning their last ends.

segments.t: Donec intrem in Sanctuárium Dei: * et intéllegam in novíssimis eórum.

content.english: 72:19 How are they brought to desolation? they have suddenly ceased to be: * they have perished by reason of their iniquity.

segments.t: Quómodo facti sunt in desolatiónem, súbito defecérunt: * periérunt propter iniquitátem suam.

content.english: 72:20 As the dream of them that awake, O Lord; * so in thy city thou shalt bring their image to nothing.

segments.t: Velut sómnium surgéntium, Dómine, * in civitáte tua imáginem ipsórum ad níhilum rédiges.

content.latin: 72:21 Quia inflammátum est cor meum, et renes mei commutáti sunt: * et ego ad níhilum redáctus sum, et nescívi.
content.english: 72:21 For my heart hath been inflamed, and my reins have been changed: * and I am brought to nothing, and I knew not.

segments.t: Quia inflammátum est cor meum, et renes mei commutáti sunt: * et ego ad níhilum redáctus sum, et nescívi.

content.latin: 72:23 Ut iuméntum factus sum apud te: * et ego semper tecum.
