segments.t: Ut iuméntum factus sum apud te: * et ego semper tecum.

content.latin: 72:24 Tenuísti manum déxteram meam: et in voluntáte tua deduxísti me, * et cum glória suscepísti me.
content.english: 72:24 Thou hast held me by my right hand; and by thy will thou hast conducted me, * and with thy glory thou hast received me.

segments.t: Tenuísti manum déxteram meam: et in voluntáte tua deduxísti me, * et cum glória suscepísti me.

content.latin: 72:25 Quid enim mihi est in cælo? * et a te quid vólui super terram?

segments.t: Quid enim mihi est in cælo? * et a te quid vólui super terram?

content.latin: 72:26 Defécit caro mea, et cor meum: * Deus cordis mei, et pars mea Deus in ætérnum.
content.english: 72:26 For thee my flesh and my heart hath fainted away: * thou art the God of my heart, and the God that is my portion for ever.

segments.t: Defécit caro mea, et cor meum: * Deus cordis mei, et pars mea Deus in ætérnum.

content.latin: 72:27 Quia ecce, qui elóngant se a te, períbunt: * perdidísti omnes, qui fornicántur abs te.

segments.t: Quia ecce, qui elóngant se a te, períbunt: * perdidísti omnes, qui fornicántur abs te.

content.latin: 72:28 Mihi autem adhærére Deo bonum est: * pónere in Dómino Deo spem meam:
content.english: 72:28 But it is good for me to adhere to my God, * to put my hope in the Lord God:

segments.t: Mihi autem adhærére Deo bonum est: * pónere in Dómino Deo spem meam:

content.latin: 73:1 Ut quid, Deus, repulísti in finem: * irátus est furor tuus super oves páscuæ tuæ?
content.english: 73:1 O God, why hast thou cast us off unto the end: * why is thy wrath enkindled against the sheep of thy pasture?

segments.t: Ut quid, Deus, repulísti in finem: * irátus est furor tuus super oves páscuæ tuæ?

content.latin: 73:2 Memor esto congregatiónis tuæ, * quam possedísti ab inítio.
content.english: 73:2 Remember thy congregation, * which thou hast possessed from the beginning.

segments.t: Memor esto congregatiónis tuæ, * quam possedísti ab inítio.

content.latin: 73:2 Redemísti virgam hereditátis tuæ: * mons Sion, in quo habitásti in eo.
content.english: 73:2 The sceptre of thy inheritance which thou hast redeemed: * mount Sion in which thou hast dwelt.

segments.t: Redemísti virgam hereditátis tuæ: * mons Sion, in quo habitásti in eo.

content.latin: 73:3 Leva manus tuas in supérbias eórum in finem: * quanta malignátus est inimícus in sancto!
content.english: 73:3 Lift up thy hands against their pride unto the end; * see what things the enemy hath done wickedly in the sanctuary.

segments.t: Leva manus tuas in supérbias eórum in finem: * quanta malignátus est inimícus in sancto!

content.latin: 73:4 Et gloriáti sunt qui odérunt te: * in médio solemnitátis tuæ.
content.english: 73:4 And they that hate thee have made their boasts, * in the midst of thy solemnity.

segments.t: Et gloriáti sunt qui odérunt te: * in médio solemnitátis tuæ.

content.latin: 73:5 Posuérunt signa sua, signa: * et non cognovérunt sicut in éxitu super summum.
content.english: 73:5 They have set up their ensigns for signs, * and they knew not both in the going out and on the highest top.

segments.t: Posuérunt signa sua, signa: * et non cognovérunt sicut in éxitu super summum.

content.latin: 73:6 Quasi in silva lignórum secúribus excidérunt iánuas eius in idípsum: * in secúri et áscia deiecérunt eam.
content.english: 73:6 As with axes in a wood of trees, they have cut down at once the gates thereof, * with axe and hatchet they have brought it down.

segments.t: Quasi in silva lignórum secúribus excidérunt iánuas eius in idípsum: * in secúri et áscia deiecérunt eam.

content.latin: 73:7 Incendérunt igni Sanctuárium tuum: * in terra polluérunt tabernáculum nóminis tui.
content.english: 73:7 They have set fire to thy sanctuary: * they have defiled the dwelling place of thy name on the earth.

segments.t: Incendérunt igni Sanctuárium tuum: * in terra polluérunt tabernáculum nóminis tui.

content.latin: 73:8 Dixérunt in corde suo cognátio eórum simul: * Quiéscere faciámus omnes dies festos Dei a terra.
content.english: 73:8 They said in their heart, the whole kindred of them together: * Let us abolish all the festival days of God from the land.

segments.t: Dixérunt in corde suo cognátio eórum simul: * Quiéscere faciámus omnes dies festos Dei a terra.

content.latin: 73:9 Signa nostra non vídimus, iam non est prophéta: * et nos non cognóscet ámplius.
content.english: 73:9 Our signs we have not seen, there is now no prophet: * and he will know us no more.

segments.t: Signa nostra non vídimus, iam non est prophéta: * et nos non cognóscet ámplius.

content.latin: 73:10 Úsquequo, Deus, improperábit inimícus: * irrítat adversárius nomen tuum in finem?
content.english: 73:10 How long, O God, shall the enemy reproach: * is the adversary to provoke thy name for ever?

segments.t: Úsquequo, Deus, improperábit inimícus: * irrítat adversárius nomen tuum in finem?

content.latin: 73:11 Ut quid avértis manum tuam, et déxteram tuam, * de médio sinu tuo in finem?
content.english: 73:11 Why dost thou turn away thy hand: and thy right hand * out of the midst of thy bosom for ever?

segments.t: Ut quid avértis manum tuam, et déxteram tuam, * de médio sinu tuo in finem?

content.latin: 73:12 Deus autem Rex noster ante sǽcula: * operátus est salútem in médio terræ.
content.english: 73:12 But God is our king before ages: * he hath wrought salvation in the midst of the earth.

segments.t: Deus autem Rex noster ante sǽcula: * operátus est salútem in médio terræ.

content.latin: 73:13 Tu confirmásti in virtúte tua mare: * contribulásti cápita dracónum in aquis.
content.english: 73:13 Thou by thy strength didst make the sea firm: * thou didst crush the heads of the dragons in the waters.

segments.t: Tu confirmásti in virtúte tua mare: * contribulásti cápita dracónum in aquis.

content.latin: 73:14 Tu confregísti cápita dracónis: * dedísti eum escam pópulis Æthíopum.
content.english: 73:14 Thou hast broken the heads of the dragon: * thou hast given him to be meat for the people of the Ethiopians.

segments.t: Tu confregísti cápita dracónis: * dedísti eum escam pópulis Æthíopum.

content.latin: 73:15 Tu dirupísti fontes, et torréntes: * tu siccásti flúvios Ethan.
content.english: 73:15 Thou hast broken up the fountains and the torrents: * thou hast dried up the Ethan rivers.

segments.t: Tu dirupísti fontes, et torréntes: * tu siccásti flúvios Ethan.

content.latin: 73:16 Tuus est dies, et tua est nox: * tu fabricátus es auróram et solem.
content.english: 73:16 Thine is the day, and thine is the night: * thou hast made the morning light and the sun.

segments.t: Tuus est dies, et tua est nox: * tu fabricátus es auróram et solem.

content.latin: 73:17 Tu fecísti omnes términos terræ: * æstátem et ver tu plasmásti ea.
content.english: 73:17 Thou hast made all the borders of the earth: * the summer and the spring were formed by thee.

segments.t: Tu fecísti omnes términos terræ: * æstátem et ver tu plasmásti ea.

content.latin: 73:18 Memor esto huius, inimícus improperávit Dómino: * et pópulus insípiens incitávit nomen tuum.
content.english: 73:18 Remember this, the enemy hath reproached the Lord: * and a foolish people hath provoked thy name.

segments.t: Memor esto huius, inimícus improperávit Dómino: * et pópulus insípiens incitávit nomen tuum.

content.latin: 73:19 Ne tradas béstiis ánimas confiténtes tibi, * et ánimas páuperum tuórum ne obliviscáris in finem.
content.english: 73:19 Deliver not up to beasts the souls that confess to thee: * and forget not to the end the souls of thy poor.

segments.t: Ne tradas béstiis ánimas confiténtes tibi, * et ánimas páuperum tuórum ne obliviscáris in finem.

content.latin: 73:20 Réspice in testaméntum tuum: * quia repléti sunt, qui obscuráti sunt terræ dómibus iniquitátum.
content.english: 73:20 Have regard to thy covenant: * for they that are the obscure of the earth have been filled with dwellings of iniquity.

segments.t: Réspice in testaméntum tuum: * quia repléti sunt, qui obscuráti sunt terræ dómibus iniquitátum.

content.latin: 73:21 Ne avertátur húmilis factus confúsus: * pauper et inops laudábunt nomen tuum.
content.english: 73:21 Let not the humble be turned away with confusion: * the poor and needy shall praise thy name.

segments.t: Ne avertátur húmilis factus confúsus: * pauper et inops laudábunt nomen tuum.

content.latin: 73:22 Exsúrge, Deus, iúdica causam tuam: * memor esto improperiórum tuórum, eórum quæ ab insipiénte sunt tota die.
content.english: 73:22 Arise, O God, judge thy own cause: * remember thy reproaches with which the foolish man hath reproached thee all the day.

segments.t: Exsúrge, Deus, iúdica causam tuam: * memor esto improperiórum tuórum, eórum quæ ab insipiénte sunt tota die.

content.latin: 73:23 Ne obliviscáris voces inimicórum tuórum: * supérbia eórum, qui te odérunt, ascéndit semper.
content.english: 73:23 Forget not the voices of thy enemies: * the pride of them that hate thee ascendeth continually.

segments.t: Ne obliviscáris voces inimicórum tuórum: * supérbia eórum, qui te odérunt, ascéndit semper.

content.latin: 136:1 Super flúmina Babylónis, illic sédimus et flévimus: * cum recordarémur Sion:
content.english: 136:1 Upon the rivers of Babylon, there we sat and wept: * when we remembered Sion:

segments.t: Super flúmina Babylónis, illic sédimus et flévimus: * cum recordarémur Sion:

content.latin: 136:2 In salícibus in médio eius, * suspéndimus órgana nostra.
content.english: 136:2 On the willows in the midst thereof * we hung up our instruments.

segments.t: In salícibus in médio eius, * suspéndimus órgana nostra.

content.latin: 136:3 Quia illic interrogavérunt nos, qui captívos duxérunt nos, * verba cantiónum:
content.english: 136:3 For there they that led us into captivity required of us * the words of songs.

segments.t: Quia illic interrogavérunt nos, qui captívos duxérunt nos, * verba cantiónum:

content.english: 136:3 And they that carried us away, said: * Sing ye to us a hymn of the songs of Sion.

segments.t: Et qui abduxérunt nos: * Hymnum cantáte nobis de cánticis Sion.

content.latin: 136:4 Quómodo cantábimus cánticum Dómini * in terra aliéna?
content.english: 136:4 How shall we sing the song of the Lord * in a strange land?

segments.t: Quómodo cantábimus cánticum Dómini * in terra aliéna?

content.latin: 136:5 Si oblítus fúero tui, Ierúsalem, * oblivióni detur déxtera mea.
content.english: 136:5 If I forget thee, O Jerusalem, * let my right hand be forgotten.

segments.t: Si oblítus fúero tui, Ierúsalem, * oblivióni detur déxtera mea.

content.latin: 136:6 Adhǽreat lingua mea fáucibus meis, * si non memínero tui:
content.english: 136:6 Let my tongue cleave to my jaws, * if I do not remember thee:

segments.t: Adhǽreat lingua mea fáucibus meis, * si non memínero tui:

segments.t: Si non proposúero Ierúsalem, * in princípio lætítiæ meæ.

content.latin: 136:7 Memor esto, Dómine, filiórum Edom, * in die Ierúsalem:
content.english: 136:7 Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom, * in the day of Jerusalem:

content.english: 136:7 Who say: Rase it, rase it, * even to the foundation thereof.

segments.t: Qui dicunt: Exinaníte, exinaníte * usque ad fundaméntum in ea.

content.english: 136:8 O daughter of Babylon, miserable: * blessed shall he be who shall repay thee thy payment which thou hast paid us.

segments.t: Fília Babylónis mísera: * beátus, qui retríbuet tibi retributiónem tuam, quam retribuísti nobis.

content.latin: 137:1 Confitébor tibi, Dómine, in toto corde meo: * quóniam audísti verba oris mei.
content.english: 137:1 I will praise thee, O Lord, with my whole heart: * for thou hast heard the words of my mouth.

segments.t: Confitébor tibi, Dómine, in toto corde meo: * quóniam audísti verba oris mei.

content.latin: 137:2 In conspéctu Angelórum psallam tibi: * adorábo ad templum sanctum tuum, et confitébor nómini tuo.
content.english: 137:2 I will sing praise to thee in the sight of the Angels: * I will worship towards thy holy temple, and I will give glory to thy name.

segments.t: In conspéctu Angelórum psallam tibi: * adorábo ad templum sanctum tuum, et confitébor nómini tuo.

content.latin: 137:3 Super misericórdia tua, et veritáte tua: * quóniam magnificásti super omne, nomen sanctum tuum.
content.english: 137:3 For thy mercy, and for thy truth: * for thou hast magnified thy holy name

segments.t: Super misericórdia tua, et veritáte tua: * quóniam magnificásti super omne, nomen sanctum tuum.

content.latin: 137:4 In quacúmque die invocávero te, exáudi me: * multiplicábis in ánima mea virtútem.
content.english: 137:4 In what day soever I shall call upon thee, hear me: * thou shalt multiply strength in my soul.

segments.t: In quacúmque die invocávero te, exáudi me: * multiplicábis in ánima mea virtútem.

content.latin: 137:5 Confiteántur tibi, Dómine, omnes reges terræ: * quia audiérunt ómnia verba oris tui:
content.english: 137:5 May all the kings of the earth give glory to thee: * for they have heard all the words of thy mouth.

segments.t: Confiteántur tibi, Dómine, omnes reges terræ: * quia audiérunt ómnia verba oris tui:

content.latin: 137:6 Et cantent in viis Dómini: * quóniam magna est glória Dómini.
content.english: 137:6 And let them sing in the ways of the Lord: * for great is the glory of the Lord.

segments.t: Et cantent in viis Dómini: * quóniam magna est glória Dómini.

content.latin: 137:7 Quóniam excélsus Dóminus, et humília réspicit: * et alta a longe cognóscit.
content.english: 137:7 For the Lord is high, and looketh on the low: * and the high he knoweth afar off.

segments.t: Quóniam excélsus Dóminus, et humília réspicit: * et alta a longe cognóscit.

content.latin: 137:8 Si ambulávero in médio tribulatiónis, vivificábis me: * et super iram inimicórum meórum extendísti manum tuam, et salvum me fecit déxtera tua.
content.english: 137:8 If I shall walk in the midst of tribulation, thou wilt quicken me: * and thou hast stretched forth thy hand against the wrath of my enemies: and thy right hand hath saved me.

segments.t: Si ambulávero in médio tribulatiónis, vivificábis me: * et super iram inimicórum meórum extendísti manum tuam, et salvum me fecit déxtera tua.

content.latin: 137:9 Dóminus retríbuet pro me: * Dómine, misericórdia tua in sǽculum: ópera mánuum tuárum ne despícias.
content.english: 137:9 The Lord will repay for me: * thy mercy, O Lord, endureth for ever: O despise not the works of thy hands.

segments.t: Dóminus retríbuet pro me: * Dómine, misericórdia tua in sǽculum: ópera mánuum tuárum ne despícias.

content.latin: Deus tuórum mílitum
content.english: O God, of those that fought thy fight,

content.english: Break every bond of sin and shame

content.english: As now we praise thy martyr's name.

content.english: He recked not of the world's allure,

content.english: But sin and pomp of sin forswore:

content.latin: Imbúta felle députans,
content.english: Knew all their gall, and passed them by,

content.latin: Pervénit ad cæléstia.
content.english: And reached the throne prepared on high.

œnas cucúrrit fórtiter,

content.latin: Et sústulit viríliter,
content.english: And bare his torments as a man:

content.english: For love of thee his blood outpoured,

content.latin: Ætérna dona póssidet.
content.english: And thus obtained the great reward.

content.latin: Ob hoc precátu súpplici
content.english: With humble voice and suppliant word

content.latin: Dimítte noxam sérvulis.

content.latin: 1:49 Quia fecit mihi magna qui potens est: * et sanctum nomen eius.

segments.t: Quia fecit mihi magna qui potens est: * et sanctum nomen eius.

content.latin: 1:50 Et misericórdia eius, a progénie in progénies: * timéntibus eum.
content.english: 1:50 And his mercy is from generation unto generations, * to them that fear him.

segments.t: Et misericórdia eius, a progénie in progénies: * timéntibus eum.

segments.t: Fecit poténtiam in brácchio suo: * dispérsit supérbos mente cordis sui.

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris: et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem: sed líbera nos a malo. Amen.
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us. And lead us not into temptation: But deliver us from evil. Amen.

content.latin: Confíteor Deo omnipoténti, beátæ Maríæ semper Vírgini, beáto Michaéli Archángelo, beáto Ioánni Baptístæ, sanctis Apóstolis Petro et Paulo, et ómnibus Sanctis, quia peccávi nimis, cogitatióne, verbo et ópere: percutit sibi pectus mea culpa, mea culpa, mea máxima culpa. Ídeo precor beátam Maríam semper Vírginem, beátum Michaélem Archángelum, beátum Ioánnem Baptístam, sanctos Apóstolos Petrum et Paulum, et omnes Sanctos, oráre pro me ad Dóminum Deum nostrum.
content.english: I confess to almighty God, to blessed Mary ever Virgin, to blessed Michael the Archangel, to blessed John the Baptist, to the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, and to all the Saints, that I have sinned exceedingly in thought, word and deed: strikes his breast through my fault, through my fault, through my most grievous fault. Therefore I beseech blessed Mary ever Virgin, blessed Michael the Archangel, blessed John the Baptist, the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, and all the Saints, to pray for me to the Lord our God.

segments.t: Confíteor Deo omnipoténti, beátæ Maríæ semper Vírgini, beáto Michaéli Archángelo, beáto Ioánni Baptístæ, sanctis Apóstolis Petro et Paulo, et ómnibus Sanctis, quia peccávi nimis, cogitatióne, verbo et ópere:

content.latin: Misereátur nostri omnípotens Deus, et dimíssis peccátis nostris, perdúcat nos ad vitam ætérnam. Amen.
content.english: May almighty God have mercy on us, forgive us our sins, and bring us to everlasting life. Amen.

content.latin: Indulgéntiam, ✠ absolutiónem et remissiónem peccatórum nostrórum tríbuat nobis omnípotens et miséricors Dóminus. Amen.
content.english: May the almighty ✠ and merciful Lord grant us pardon, absolution and remission of our sins. Amen.

content.latin: 69:2 Deus, in adiutórium meum inténde: * Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.
content.english: 69:2 O God, come to my assistance; * O Lord, make haste to help me.

segments.t: Deus, in adiutórium meum inténde: * Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.

content.latin: 69:3 Confundántur et revereántur, * qui quærunt ánimam meam.
content.english: 69:3 Let them be confounded and ashamed * that seek my soul:

segments.t: Confundántur et revereántur, * qui quærunt ánimam meam.

content.latin: 69:4 Avertántur retrórsum, et erubéscant, * qui volunt mihi mala.
content.english: 69:4 Let them be turned backward, and blush for shame * that desire evils to me:

segments.t: Avertántur retrórsum, et erubéscant, * qui volunt mihi mala.

content.latin: 69:4 Avertántur statim erubescéntes, * qui dicunt mihi: Euge, euge.
content.english: 69:4 Let them be presently turned away blushing for shame * that say to me: ’T is well, ’t is well.

segments.t: Avertántur statim erubescéntes, * qui dicunt mihi: Euge, euge.

content.latin: 69:5 Exsúltent et læténtur in te omnes qui quærunt te, * et dicant semper: Magnificétur Dóminus: qui díligunt salutáre tuum.
content.english: 69:5 Let all that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee; * and let such as love thy salvation say always: The Lord be magnified.

segments.t: Exsúltent et læténtur in te omnes qui quærunt te, * et dicant semper: Magnificétur Dóminus: qui díligunt salutáre tuum.

content.latin: 69:6 Ego vero egénus, et pauper sum: * Deus, ádiuva me.
content.english: 69:6 But I am needy and poor; * O God, help me.

segments.t: Ego vero egénus, et pauper sum: * Deus, ádiuva me.

content.latin: 69:6 Adiútor meus, et liberátor meus es tu: * Dómine, ne moréris.
content.english: 69:6 Thou art my helper and my deliverer: * O Lord, make no delay.

segments.t: Adiútor meus, et liberátor meus es tu: * Dómine, ne moréris.

Psalmus 70(1-12)

content.latin: 70:1 In te, Dómine, sperávi, non confúndar in ætérnum: * in iustítia tua líbera me, et éripe me.
content.english: 70:1 In thee, O Lord, I have hoped, let me never be put to confusion: * deliver me in thy justice, and rescue me.

segments.t: In te, Dómine, sperávi, non confúndar in ætérnum: * in iustítia tua líbera me, et éripe me.

content.latin: 70:2 Inclína ad me aurem tuam, * et salva me.
content.english: 70:2 Incline thy ear unto me, * and save me.

segments.t: Inclína ad me aurem tuam, * et salva me.

content.latin: 70:3 Esto mihi in Deum protectórem, et in locum munítum: * ut salvum me fácias,
content.english: 70:3 Be thou unto me a God, a protector, and a place of strength: * that thou mayst make me safe.

segments.t: Esto mihi in Deum protectórem, et in locum munítum: * ut salvum me fácias,

content.latin: 70:3 Quóniam firmaméntum meum, * et refúgium meum es tu.
content.english: 70:3 For thou art my firmament * and my refuge.

segments.t: Quóniam firmaméntum meum, * et refúgium meum es tu.

content.latin: 70:4 Deus meus, éripe me de manu peccatóris, * et de manu contra legem agéntis et iníqui:
content.english: 70:4 Deliver me, O my God, out of the hand of the sinner, * and out of the hand of the transgressor of the law and of the unjust.

segments.t: Deus meus, éripe me de manu peccatóris, * et de manu contra legem agéntis et iníqui:

content.latin: 70:5 Quóniam tu es patiéntia mea, Dómine: * Dómine, spes mea a iuventúte mea.
content.english: 70:5 For thou art my patience, O Lord: * my hope, O Lord, from my youth.

segments.t: Quóniam tu es patiéntia mea, Dómine: * Dómine, spes mea a iuventúte mea.

content.latin: 70:6 In te confirmátus sum ex útero: * de ventre matris meæ tu es protéctor meus.
content.english: 70:6 By thee have I been confirmed from the womb: * from my mother’s womb thou art my protector.

segments.t: In te confirmátus sum ex útero: * de ventre matris meæ tu es protéctor meus.

content.latin: 70:7 In te cantátio mea semper: * tamquam prodígium factus sum multis: et tu adiútor fortis.
content.english: 70:7 Of thee shall I continually sing: * I am become unto many as a wonder, but thou art a strong helper.

segments.t: In te cantátio mea semper: * tamquam prodígium factus sum multis: et tu adiútor fortis.

content.latin: 70:8 Repleátur os meum laude, ut cantem glóriam tuam: * tota die magnitúdinem tuam.
content.english: 70:8 Let my mouth be filled with praise, that I may sing thy glory; * thy greatness all the day long.

segments.t: Repleátur os meum laude, ut cantem glóriam tuam: * tota die magnitúdinem tuam.

content.latin: 70:9 Ne proícias me in témpore senectútis: * cum defécerit virtus mea, ne derelínquas me.
content.english: 70:9 Cast me not off in the time of old age: * when my strength shall fail, do not thou forsake me.

segments.t: Ne proícias me in témpore senectútis: * cum defécerit virtus mea, ne derelínquas me.

content.latin: 70:10 Quia dixérunt inimíci mei mihi: * et qui custodiébant ánimam meam, consílium fecérunt in unum.
content.english: 70:10 For my enemies have spoken against me; * and they that watched my soul have consulted together,

segments.t: Quia dixérunt inimíci mei mihi: * et qui custodiébant ánimam meam, consílium fecérunt in unum.

content.latin: 70:11 Dicéntes: Deus derelíquit eum, persequímini, et comprehéndite eum: * quia non est qui erípiat.
content.english: 70:11 Saying: God hath forsaken him: pursue and take him, * for there is none to deliver him.

segments.t: Dicéntes: Deus derelíquit eum, persequímini, et comprehéndite eum: * quia non est qui erípiat.

content.latin: 70:12 Deus, ne elongéris a me: * Deus meus, in auxílium meum réspice.
content.english: 70:12 O God, be not thou far from me: * O my God, make haste to my help.

segments.t: Deus, ne elongéris a me: * Deus meus, in auxílium meum réspice.

Psalmus 70(13-24)

content.latin: 70:13 Confundántur, et defíciant detrahéntes ánimæ meæ: * operiántur confusióne, et pudóre qui quærunt mala mihi.
content.english: 70:13 Let them be confounded and come to nothing that detract my soul; * let them be covered with confusion and shame that seek my hurt.

segments.t: Confundántur, et defíciant detrahéntes ánimæ meæ: * operiántur confusióne, et pudóre qui quærunt mala mihi.

content.latin: 70:14 Ego autem semper sperábo: * et adíciam super omnem laudem tuam.
content.english: 70:14 But I will always hope; * and will add to all thy praise.

segments.t: Ego autem semper sperábo: * et adíciam super omnem laudem tuam.

content.latin: 70:15 Os meum annuntiábit iustítiam tuam: * tota die salutáre tuum.
content.english: 70:15 My mouth shall shew forth thy justice; * thy salvation all the day long.

segments.t: Os meum annuntiábit iustítiam tuam: * tota die salutáre tuum.

content.latin: 70:16 Quóniam non cognóvi litteratúram, introíbo in poténtias Dómini: * Dómine, memorábor iustítiæ tuæ solíus.
content.english: 70:16 Because I have not known learning, I will enter into the powers of the Lord: * O Lord, I will be mindful of thy justice alone.

segments.t: Quóniam non cognóvi litteratúram, introíbo in poténtias Dómini: * Dómine, memorábor iustítiæ tuæ solíus.

content.latin: 70:17 Deus, docuísti me a iuventúte mea: * et usque nunc pronuntiábo mirabília tua.
content.english: 70:17 Thou hast taught me, O God, from my youth: * and till now I will declare thy wonderful works.

segments.t: Deus, docuísti me a iuventúte mea: * et usque nunc pronuntiábo mirabília tua.

content.latin: 70:18 Et usque in senéctam et sénium: * Deus, ne derelínquas me,
content.english: 70:18 And unto old age and grey hairs: * O God, forsake me not,

segments.t: Et usque in senéctam et sénium: * Deus, ne derelínquas me,

content.latin: 70:18 Donec annúntiem brácchium tuum * generatióni omni, quæ ventúra est:
content.english: 70:18 Until I shew forth thy arm * to all the generation that is to come:

segments.t: Donec annúntiem brácchium tuum * generatióni omni, quæ ventúra est:

content.latin: 70:19 Poténtiam tuam, et iustítiam tuam, Deus, usque in altíssima, quæ fecísti magnália: * Deus, quis símilis tibi?
content.english: 70:19 Thy power, and thy justice, O God, even to the highest great things thou hast done: * O God, who is like to thee?

segments.t: Poténtiam tuam, et iustítiam tuam, Deus, usque in altíssima, quæ fecísti magnália: * Deus, quis símilis tibi?

content.latin: 70:20 Quantas ostendísti mihi tribulatiónes multas et malas: et convérsus vivificásti me: * et de abýssis terræ íterum reduxísti me:
content.english: 70:20 How great troubles hast thou shewn me, many and grievous: and turning thou hast brought me to life, * and hast brought me back again from the depths of the earth:

segments.t: Quantas ostendísti mihi tribulatiónes multas et malas: et convérsus vivificásti me: * et de abýssis terræ íterum reduxísti me:

content.latin: 70:21 Multiplicásti magnificéntiam tuam: * et convérsus consolátus es me.
content.english: 70:21 Thou hast multiplied thy magnificence; * and turning to me thou hast comforted me.

segments.t: Multiplicásti magnificéntiam tuam: * et convérsus consolátus es me.

content.latin: 70:22 Nam et ego confitébor tibi in vasis psalmi veritátem tuam: * Deus, psallam tibi in cíthara, Sanctus Israël.
content.english: 70:22 For I will also confess to thee thy truth with the instruments of psaltery: * O God, I will sing to thee with the harp,

segments.t: Nam et ego confitébor tibi in vasis psalmi veritátem tuam: * Deus, psallam tibi in cíthara, Sanctus Israël.

content.latin: 70:23 Exsultábunt lábia mea cum cantávero tibi: * et ánima mea, quam redemísti.
content.english: 70:23 My lips shall greatly rejoice, when I shall sing to thee; * and my soul which thou hast redeemed.

segments.t: Exsultábunt lábia mea cum cantávero tibi: * et ánima mea, quam redemísti.

content.latin: 70:24 Sed et lingua mea tota die meditábitur iustítiam tuam: * cum confúsi et revériti fúerint, qui quærunt mala mihi.
content.english: 70:24 Yea and my tongue shall meditate on thy justice all the day; * when they shall be confounded and put to shame that seek evils to me.

segments.t: Sed et lingua mea tota die meditábitur iustítiam tuam: * cum confúsi et revériti fúerint, qui quærunt mala mihi.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Salva nos, Dómine, vigilántes, custódi nos dormiéntes; ut vigilémus cum Christo, et requiescámus in pace.
content.english: Ant. Protect us, Lord, while we are awake and safeguard us while we sleep; that we may keep watch with Christ, and rest in peace.

segments.t: Ant.
Salva nos, Dómine, vigilántes, custódi nos dormiéntes; ut vigilémus cum Christo, et requiescámus in pace.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

segments.t: Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

segments.t: Et clamor meus ad te véniat.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Vísita, quǽsumus, Dómine, habitatiónem istam, et omnes insídias inimíci ab ea longe repélle: Ángeli tui sancti hábitent in ea, qui nos in pace custódiant; et benedíctio tua sit super nos semper.
content.english: Visit, we beseech thee, O Lord, this dwelling, and drive far from it the snares of the enemy; let thy holy angels dwell herein to preserve us in peace, and let thy blessing be always upon us.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

segments.t: Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

segments.t: Et clamor meus ad te véniat.

content.latin: ℣. Benedicámus Dómino.
content.english: ℣. Let us bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedicámus Dómino.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: Benedictio. Benedícat et custódiat nos omnípotens et miséricors Dóminus, ✠ Pater, et Fílius, et Spíritus Sanctus.
content.english: Benediction. The almighty and merciful Lord, ✠ the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, bless us and keep us.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Benedícat et custódiat nos omnípotens et miséricors Dóminus, ✠ Pater, et Fílius, et Spíritus Sanctus.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: Salve, Regína, mater misericórdiæ;
content.english: Hail holy Queen, Mother of Mercy,

content.latin: vita, dulcédo et spes nóstra, salve.
content.english: our life, our sweetness, and our hope.

content.latin: Ad te clamámus éxsules fílii Hevæ.
content.english: To thee do we cry, poor banished children of Eve.

content.latin: Ad te suspirámus geméntes et flentes
content.english: To thee do we send up our sighs, mourning and weeping

content.latin: In hac lacrimárum valle.
content.english: In this valley of tears.

content.latin: Eia ergo, advocáta nostra,
content.english: Turn then, most gracious Advocate,

content.latin: illos tuos misericórdes óculos ad nos convérte.
content.english: thine eyes of mercy toward us.

content.latin: Et Iesum, benedíctum fructum ventris tui,
content.english: And after this our exile show unto us

content.latin: nobis post hoc exsílium osténde.
content.english: the blessed fruit of thy womb, Jesus.

content.latin: O clemens, o pia, o dulcis Virgo María.
content.english: O clement, O loving, O sweet Virgin Mary.

content.latin: ℣. Ora pro nobis, sancta Dei Génetrix.
content.english: ℣. Pray for us, O Holy Mother of God.

segments.t: Ora pro nobis, sancta Dei Génetrix.

content.latin: ℟. Ut digni efficiámur promissiónibus Christi.
content.english: ℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

segments.t: Ut digni efficiámur promissiónibus Christi.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui gloriósæ Vírginis Matris Maríæ corpus et ánimam, ut dignum Fílii tui habitáculum éffici mererétur, Spíritu Sancto cooperánte, præparásti: da, ut, cuius commemoratióne lætámur, eius pia intercessióne, ab instántibus malis et a morte perpétua liberémur. Per eúndem Christum Dóminum nostrum. Amen.
content.english: O almighty, everlasting God, who by the cooperation of the Holy Spirit, didst prepare the body and soul of Mary, glorious Virgin and Mother, to become a worthy dwelling for Thy Son; grant that we who rejoice in her commemoration may, by her gracious intercession, be delivered from present evils and from everlasting death. Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Divínum auxílium ✠ máneat semper nobíscum.
content.english: ℣. May the divine assistance ✠ remain with us always.

segments.t: Divínum auxílium ✠ máneat semper nobíscum.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.
